title: The Atlas of Lost Letters
tagline: Find the stories the city tried to forget.
premise: Mira discovers a wax-sealed letter addressed to someone who vanished from the municipal register.

chapters.title: A Letter Without a Name
chapters.intro: In the closed wing of the municipal archive, Mira finds a letter dated tomorrow but stamped forty years ago. A single hand-drawn street is visible under the envelope flap.
chapters.objective: Decide how to examine the mysterious letter.

choices.label: Study the seal
choices.outcome: Mira angles the wax beneath the lamp. The imprint matches the seal of a long-disbanded street survey office. Its records were relocated after the flood.
choices.memoryHint: The seal points to the old survey office.

choices.label: Read the watermark
choices.outcome: Held to the window, the paper shows the watermark of a mill that closed decades ago. Mira traces a tiny star beside the maker’s crest.
choices.memoryHint: The watermark reveals an old paper mill.

chapters.title: The Missing Address
chapters.intro: The letter names Bellwether Lane, but no modern map lists it. Mira unfurls a water-damaged survey of the lower city and finds a blank rectangle where the lane should be.
chapters.objective: Choose the first lead to follow.

choices.label: Check the flood records
choices.outcome: The flood ledger lists three houses that were quietly removed from later editions. Mira notices a clerk’s initials repeated beside every correction.
choices.memoryHint: The clerk’s initials connect the missing houses.

choices.label: Visit the lane at dawn
choices.outcome: At sunrise the shape of Bellwether Lane is visible in the old paving stones. Mira finds a brass number plate embedded beneath new concrete.
choices.memoryHint: The hidden number plate confirms the lane existed.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Maps
chapters.intro: In the mapmaker’s workshop, an elderly caretaker offers a choice: preserve the secret archive as it is, or publish its existence to descendants of the missing residents.
chapters.objective: Choose how to honor the history.

choices.label: Protect the fragile originals
choices.outcome: Mira photographs each sheet, places the maps in climate-safe storage, and opens a private register for descendants. The evidence survives without inviting damage.
choices.memoryHint: The archive is protected and descendants are invited.

choices.label: Share the discovery publicly
choices.outcome: Mira prepares a careful public notice with private details removed. A family contacts the archive carrying the missing final map.
choices.memoryHint: A public notice reunites the missing map.

chapters.title: The Atlas Opens
chapters.intro: The last letter contains no treasure, only a request: return the street’s names to the city memory. Mira lays the restored atlas beside the new address register.
chapters.objective: Decide what the atlas becomes.

choices.label: Create a public exhibition
choices.outcome: The city opens a small exhibition of recovered addresses. Visitors add their own memories, and Bellwether Lane finds its place again.
choices.memoryHint: Bellwether Lane enters the city exhibition.

choices.label: Build a family archive
choices.outcome: Mira creates a searchable archive for families and sends the first restored letter to its rightful descendants. The atlas becomes a living record.
choices.memoryHint: The restored letters find their families.

chapters.title: The Lantern Below
chapters.setting: A second letter, a different ink
chapters.intro: Three weeks after the atlas opens, a courier delivers an envelope with no return address. The wax is blue, the date is tomorrow, and the street drawn inside runs beneath Bellwether Lane — a passage that appears in no survey Mira can find.

echoes.mira_c1_a: You trusted the seal once before. This imprint is sharper, as if pressed by a steadier hand.
echoes.mira_c1_b: You read the watermark last time. This paper carries none, which is its own kind of answer.

chapters.objective: Decide how to test the second letter.

choices.label: Compare the two seals
choices.outcome: Side by side, the new seal is a copy with one deliberate flaw. Mira recognizes it as a surveyor's mark of correction — someone is asking to be found, not misled.
choices.memoryHint: A corrected seal asks to be found.

choices.label: Test the ink against the atlas
choices.outcome: The ink matches a batch used for official corrections after the flood. In the margin, in the same hand: 'The lane beneath the lane.' Mira feels the floor of the archive shift.
choices.memoryHint: Marginal ink points beneath the lane.

chapters.title: The Street Under Glass
chapters.setting: A hearing room with too many maps
chapters.intro: A developer's plan would drive a service pipe straight through the recovered lane. The atlas is the only document proving the street existed. The hearing gives Mira ten minutes and asks for a single, usable exhibit.

echoes.mira_c3_a: You kept the fragile maps safe. Their safety is now being weighed against their usefulness.
echoes.mira_c3_b: You published the discovery. The hearing room is crowded with people who read your notice.

chapters.objective: Choose how the atlas enters the public record.

choices.label: Present the atlas as evidence
choices.outcome: Mira shows the survey and the correction side by side. The hearing grants a temporary hold, on condition that engineers may handle the originals under supervision.
choices.memoryHint: The atlas wins a supervised hold.

choices.label: Bring the residents' own maps
choices.outcome: Neighbors unfold hand-drawn copies of the lane, each with a different doorway remembered. The hearing cannot dismiss a street that forty people can draw from memory.
choices.memoryHint: Residents' maps delay the pipeline.

chapters.title: The Names We Keep
chapters.intro: Ivo, the clerk's great-grandson, asks Mira to leave one name out of the record: the clerk who erased the lane. He says the family has carried the shame long enough, and that some inheritances should be allowed to end.

echoes.mira_c4_a: Your exhibition invited visitors to add their own memories. Ivo has come to add — and to subtract.
echoes.mira_c4_b: Your family archive promised context, not absolution. Ivo is testing that promise.

chapters.objective: Decide how the erasure is remembered.

choices.label: Publish the clerk's record with context
choices.outcome: Mira writes the erasure into the atlas beside the lane it hid, and the pressure the clerk was under. Ivo reads it twice, then asks to add a note in his own hand.
choices.memoryHint: The erasure is recorded with context.

choices.label: Let the family write the first label
choices.outcome: Ivo writes: 'Removed under orders; remembered by those who stayed.' The atlas gains a voice Mira could not have written, and one name quietly returns.
choices.memoryHint: The family names the erasure themselves.

chapters.title: The Atlas Answers
chapters.intro: The city offers the atlas a permanent home, on one condition. It must become either a protected artifact or a working map that anyone may annotate. Mira has one evening, a lamp, and every choice she has made behind her.

echoes.mira_c2_a: The flood ledger taught you that every correction leaves a trace. This choice will leave one too.
echoes.mira_c2_b: You once stood where the lane used to be. The city is asking whether others should stand there too.

chapters.objective: Decide what the atlas becomes next.

choices.label: Keep it as a protected artifact
choices.outcome: The atlas goes behind glass with a complete digital companion. Scholars study it; children press their hands to the case. It survives intact, and at a distance, and Mira learns to accept that.
choices.memoryHint: The atlas is preserved as evidence.

choices.label: Make it a living public map
choices.outcome: The atlas becomes a working map anyone can annotate. Some entries are wrong within a month; others are the truest lines in the room. Mira leaves the door unlocked.
choices.memoryHint: The atlas becomes a shared, living map.

chapters.title: The Right to a Blank Space
chapters.setting: Six months later, the reading-room table
chapters.intro:
The atlas now has a permanent place in the city, but the correction requests still arrive in ordinary envelopes. One is from Ivo, asking for an address associated with his family to be removed from the public index. It is accurate. That is the difficulty.

Across the table, Mira sets down the old correction slip she has carried since her first cataloguing mistake. She had expected Ivo to admire the admission. Instead he asks, gently, why she needs him to witness it. The room grows quiet enough to hear the radiator.

Removing a public reference need not destroy the underlying evidence. Leaving it visible need not expose every detail. Neither route will settle the larger disagreement about who the archive serves. Mira asks Ivo to help choose a process, rather than become its example.
chapters.objective: Decide how to handle an accurate record whose visibility is contested.

echoes.mira_c8_a: The atlas is protected behind glass. Ivo's request concerns the public index, where protection of paper has not protected every person.
echoes.mira_c8_b: The map accepts public annotations. Ivo asks whether the right to add a name includes a meaningful way to ask for its removal.

choices.label: Restrict the public entry with a review date
choices.outcome: Mira and Ivo agree to remove the address from open search while retaining a documented restricted record. They write down who may request access and when the restriction will be reconsidered. Some researchers object to the extra step. Ivo does not thank her for granting an exception; he asks her to make the process available to others. Mira agrees, without putting his name on the new form.
choices.memoryHint: A restricted public entry retains its evidence and a review date.

choices.label: Keep the entry with a resident-written correction
choices.outcome: Ivo writes a short statement separating the address from the conclusions visitors have drawn about his family. Mira places it beside the index entry and removes unnecessary identifying details. The entry remains searchable, and Ivo knows that some readers will skip his statement. They record that limit explicitly. Mira stops calling visibility an uncomplicated gift.
choices.memoryHint: The public entry carries the resident's own account and its limits.

chapters.title: A Key That Is Not Hers
chapters.intro:
The correction process is ready for its first review. An adult resident arrives while Mira is still arranging the chairs and asks who will make the final decision. Mira almost answers with her job title. Ivo is beside the kettle, not at the head of the table.

On a sheet between them are two workable arrangements: a small paid resident panel with rotating seats, or an archive-led service with published decisions and an independent appeal. Both need funding. Both can exclude people who cannot attend at the offered time. Neither makes Mira unnecessary, which she discovers is part of what she has been afraid of.

She moves her correction slip out of the display folder. It can remain evidence of a mistake without becoming the centre of someone else's meeting.
chapters.objective: Choose who holds authority over future corrections.

echoes.mira_c9_a: The first restricted entry needs a review. A promise written on a form will mean little unless someone besides Mira can challenge it.
echoes.mira_c9_b: The resident-written account is public. Now the archive must decide who can question the way it is presented.

choices.label: Fund a rotating resident review panel
choices.outcome: Mira reallocates part of the exhibition budget to paid review sessions, remote submissions and rotating resident seats. The exhibition becomes smaller; the minutes become longer. Ivo declines a permanent place and nominates another adult resident instead. At the first meeting, a decision goes against Mira's recommendation. She records it accurately and hands the next speaker the key to the room.
choices.memoryHint: Residents gain paid, rotating authority over the correction process.

choices.label: Keep archive stewardship with an independent appeal
choices.outcome: Mira publishes the criteria, response times and reasons for decisions, then negotiates an appeal route outside her own team. Staff retain responsibility and cannot point to unpaid residents when a decision is unpopular. The first appeal overturns her wording. She changes it before opening time. The atlas remains under her care, but no longer only on her terms.
choices.memoryHint: Archive decisions become published, accountable and independently appealable.

title: The Last Light Buoy
tagline: Follow a signal beyond the last light buoy.
premise: A deep-sea listening station records a melody with no known biological source.

chapters.title: An Unlisted Frequency
chapters.intro: Jonah’s hydrophone captures three repeating notes outside the shipping lanes. The buoy log says the transmission came from a sensor that was disconnected last winter.
chapters.objective: Choose the safest first investigation.

choices.label: Compare the recordings
choices.outcome: The frequencies fit the resonance of an old underwater cable rather than a sea creature. Jonah marks a corridor across the seabed.
choices.memoryHint: The sound follows an old cable corridor.

choices.label: Inspect the buoy log
choices.outcome: A maintenance entry references a replacement beacon never installed. Jonah finds a handwritten coordinate erased from the electronic log.
choices.memoryHint: The log reveals an erased coordinate.

chapters.title: The Lantern Current
chapters.intro: A research vessel arrives at the coordinate as weather turns. The crew has time for one careful scan before the swell grows dangerous.
chapters.objective: Select a noninvasive survey method.

choices.label: Deploy the side-scan sonar
choices.outcome: The scan reveals a metal frame resting near a protected reef. Jonah keeps the vessel well clear of the coral.
choices.memoryHint: A submerged frame appears near the reef.

choices.label: Use the passive microphones
choices.outcome: A faint second rhythm emerges whenever the tide rises. Jonah calculates an exact twenty-minute acoustic window.
choices.memoryHint: The tide controls the mysterious rhythm.

chapters.title: The Silent Platform
chapters.intro: The signal leads to a weather platform abandoned after a historic storm. Inside its recovered records is an unfinished community warning system.
chapters.objective: Choose what the research team should restore.

choices.label: Repair the warning relay
choices.outcome: Jonah tests the relay with simulated storm data before it returns to service. The coastal towns regain an early-warning channel.
choices.memoryHint: The warning relay is safely restored.

choices.label: Recover the platform’s logs
choices.outcome: The old logs identify a pattern of dangerous swell long missed by regional maps. Jonah shares the findings with local harbor teams.
choices.memoryHint: The lost swell data becomes public safety guidance.

chapters.title: A Light for the Coast
chapters.intro: At dawn, the repaired coastal network answers the mystery: the notes were a test sequence sent by a forgotten safety system. The water is quiet again.
chapters.objective: Choose how to carry the discovery forward.

choices.label: Build a community listening station
choices.outcome: Jonah opens the first listening session to harbor volunteers, turning an eerie signal into a shared safety tool.
choices.memoryHint: A community station begins listening.

choices.label: Publish an open field guide
choices.outcome: Jonah writes an accessible guide to interpreting coastal sounds, and the research crew trains the next generation of observers.
choices.memoryHint: The discovery becomes an open field guide.

chapters.title: The Second Bell
chapters.setting: A buoy that should be silent
chapters.intro: Two months after the coastal network answers, a second pattern surfaces twenty miles north. The notes are the same three, but slower, and they come from a buoy the harbor recorded as decommissioned. A fishing crew heard them first.

echoes.jonah_c1_a: You followed the old cable corridor once. This signal runs parallel to it, then turns away.
echoes.jonah_c1_b: You found an erased coordinate in the log. The new signal sits almost exactly where it would have been.

chapters.objective: Choose the first response to the new signal.

choices.label: Charter a cautious survey
choices.outcome: Jonah takes a small crew out at slack tide. The sonar finds a second frame, older than the first, wrapped in fishing line. He marks it and turns back before the weather closes.
choices.memoryHint: A second frame lies north of the reef.

choices.label: Ask the harbor to log reports
choices.outcome: Jonah gives the crews a simple listening card. Within a week, three boats report the same three notes at different tides. The pattern is bigger than one station.
choices.memoryHint: Harbor crews map the second signal.

chapters.title: Weather From the Wrong Side
chapters.intro: A fast low-pressure system deepens overnight. The restored old relay reads a swell two meters higher than the official forecast. If Jonah relays it, the harbor may close unnecessarily. If he waits, the window closes with the crews still out.

echoes.jonah_c3_a: You repaired the relay with simulated storms first. Its first real disagreement is now in front of you.
echoes.jonah_c3_b: You recovered the old swell logs. The pattern they describe is forming again.

chapters.objective: Decide what to do with the uncertified warning.

choices.label: Relay it with clear uncertainty
choices.outcome: Jonah sends the old relay's reading labeled 'unverified, older instrument'. Two crews come in early. The storm arrives late, but it arrives, and no one argues about the label.
choices.memoryHint: An uncertain warning is relayed honestly.

choices.label: Verify with two independent stations
choices.outcome: Jonah spends an hour cross-checking buoys. The delayed warning is confirmed but late. One crew rides out the swell; the harbor keeps a new rule about verification windows.
choices.memoryHint: Verification costs an hour of warning.

chapters.title: The Keepers of the Sound
chapters.intro: A volunteer at the community station hears a rhythmic knock beneath the shipping lane — not the old melody, but a hand on metal. The logs show no vessel. Jonah has one boat, one radio, and a decision about whose voice counts.

echoes.jonah_c4_a: You turned the signal into a shared safety tool. Tonight the tool is being used by someone who has never heard the melody.
echoes.jonah_c4_b: Your field guide taught the coast to listen. A volunteer heard what the instruments almost missed.

chapters.objective: Choose how to answer the knock.

choices.label: Send the nearest boat
choices.outcome: Jonah dispatches a harbor launch to the coordinates. They find a diver tangled in a mooring line, alive and furious. The knock was a wrench against a hull.
choices.memoryHint: The knock was a diver in trouble.

choices.label: Coordinate with the coast guard
choices.outcome: Jonah relays the bearing and keeps the channel open while the coast guard launches. The rescue is slower to start and cleaner to run, and the volunteer hears the whole thing.
choices.memoryHint: The station becomes a relay for rescue.

chapters.title: All the Lights at Once
chapters.intro: The melody is finally explained: a maintenance handshake from a network nobody switched off. The harbor can restore every buoy to full automation, or keep the chain as a listening commons run by volunteers. The tide is turning either way.

echoes.jonah_c2_a: The sonar showed you a frame near the reef. Automation would wake every frame in the chain.
echoes.jonah_c2_b: The tide once gave you a twenty-minute window. The volunteers have learned to wait for it.

chapters.objective: Choose what the coastal network becomes.

choices.label: Restore the full automated chain
choices.outcome: Every buoy answers at once, a clean grid of light along the coast. The volunteers keep a channel for what the machines miss. Jonah sleeps through a full night for the first time in months.
choices.memoryHint: The buoy chain is fully restored.

choices.label: Keep it a listening commons
choices.outcome: The chain stays half-wild, maintained by hand and heard by many. It misses some alarms and catches others no grid would. Jonah calls it a coast that pays attention.
choices.memoryHint: The coast keeps a listening commons.

chapters.title: The Sound He Missed
chapters.setting: The harbor office after a calm night
chapters.intro:
A routine review finds a warning that reached the harbor eight minutes late. No one was injured, and the crew involved has asked that its name stay out of the public discussion. A graph on Jonah's desk makes the delay look obvious. The shift log does not. Three adults were balancing maintenance, radio traffic and a report that changed twice.

Nessa brings two mugs and no prepared accusation. She asks Jonah why his signature appears on every exception, even on shifts when he was not there. He begins explaining the network, then hears the question he has avoided: has he built a safety system, or a system that waits for him?

The team can begin by publishing a de-identified incident account, or by running a closed rehearsal before releasing the findings. Either path must name the delay without turning one tired operator into the explanation.
chapters.objective: Choose how the team learns from a near miss without blaming a single person.

echoes.jonah_c8_a: The automated chain records precise timestamps. Its clean graph still cannot explain what the operators understood at the time.
echoes.jonah_c8_b: The listening commons catches subtle sounds. Its hand-written handovers also show how easily responsibility can become unclear.

choices.label: Publish a de-identified incident review
choices.outcome: Jonah removes identifying details with the crew's agreement and publishes the timeline, uncertainties and proposed changes. Harbor operators correct two of his assumptions before the review is final. A headline calls it a failure; the report resists that simple ending. Nessa adds a plain explanation of who can act during an ambiguous warning, without waiting for Jonah's signature.
choices.memoryHint: The near miss becomes a public account of system conditions, not personal blame.

choices.label: Rehearse the handover before publishing findings
choices.outcome: The team runs the same changing reports through a tabletop exercise. Jonah is assigned to observe without answering. Twice, the room turns toward him; twice, Nessa redirects the question to the written procedure. Their eventual report includes the exercise's limitations and a date for publication. The delay buys useful understanding, but the crew has to wait longer to see what changed.
choices.memoryHint: A closed rehearsal exposes dependence on Jonah before findings are published.

chapters.title: The Watch He Can Leave
chapters.intro:
The revised plan has one unresolved line: who may stop operations when observations conflict? A single coordinator offers consistency but can become a bottleneck. Distributed authority lets trained crews act sooner, at the cost of decisions that neighboring crews may not share.

Nessa asks Jonah to take his first uninterrupted leave since the station reopened. He has packed a receiver with the volume turned down, as if that were different from bringing it. Beside it lies a blank listening card. For once, he has no observation to add.

The choice before the harbor is not whether to care about safety. It is how responsibility is distributed, how disagreements are reviewed, and whether the people doing the work can rest without asking someone else to become indispensable.
chapters.objective: Choose a durable allocation of decision-making responsibility.

echoes.jonah_c9_a: The published review promises a clearer authority structure. Readers will be able to compare the promise with the eventual handover.
echoes.jonah_c9_b: The rehearsal showed how often the room waited for Jonah. The new handover must work while he remains silent.

choices.label: Give trained crews shared stop authority
choices.outcome: The harbor establishes shared stop authority within documented limits, accompanied by paid training and review of disagreements. One cautious closure later proves unnecessary. Jonah supports the crew's decision anyway, then helps adjust the training rather than remove their authority. Nessa takes the receiver out of his bag and leaves the blank card. He goes home to buy bread.
choices.memoryHint: Trained crews share stop authority, with paid practice and accountable review.

choices.label: Create a staffed coordinating watch
choices.outcome: The harbor funds a rotating coordinating watch with a named backup on every shift. Crews have an explicit escalation path, and no shift belongs permanently to Jonah. The rota costs money that would have bought another sensor. On the first morning off, he checks the clock rather than the receiver. Someone else signs the handover, and the coast continues without his permission.
choices.memoryHint: A funded rotating watch replaces dependence on one indispensable expert.

title: The Blue Gallery
tagline: A hidden painting is waiting to be seen.
premise: Elara finds a second portrait beneath a recently donated canvas.

chapters.title: Under the Varnish
chapters.intro: Elara inspects a portrait donated to the Blue Gallery. Under raking light, the paint reveals a second pair of eyes and a small gold signature.
chapters.objective: Choose how to investigate without harming the canvas.

choices.label: Take an infrared image
choices.outcome: The scan reveals a different composition under the visible paint. Elara records the results before touching the varnish.
choices.memoryHint: Infrared imaging reveals a hidden composition.

choices.label: Research the frame
choices.outcome: A conservator’s note inside the old frame mentions an unnamed artist who worked in the museum after hours.
choices.memoryHint: The frame points to an overlooked artist.

chapters.title: The Painter’s Notebook
chapters.intro: The museum’s ledger contains a blue-stained notebook with sketches of the hidden portrait. Several pages were cut out before it entered the collection.
chapters.objective: Choose a trail to follow.

choices.label: Study the pigment samples
choices.outcome: Elara discovers the same rare cobalt mixture on a second canvas. The two works may belong to one unfinished series.
choices.memoryHint: Two canvases share the same unusual pigment.

choices.label: Interview the retired registrar
choices.outcome: The registrar recalls a quiet apprentice whose work was repeatedly attributed to others. She offers an old exhibition photograph.
choices.memoryHint: An old photo identifies the overlooked apprentice.

chapters.title: A Name Returned
chapters.intro: With enough evidence to revise the museum record, Elara must decide how to explain the layered painting without erasing either artist’s work.
chapters.objective: Choose how to present the restoration.

choices.label: Show both layers side by side
choices.outcome: The gallery prepares a display of noninvasive scans, revealing the hidden artist while preserving the visible work.
choices.memoryHint: Visitors can see both layers without damage.

choices.label: Reattribute the catalog entry
choices.outcome: Elara submits a documented provenance review; the museum adds the apprentice’s name and the uncertainty of the evidence.
choices.memoryHint: The catalog credits the overlooked artist.

chapters.title: The Blue Room
chapters.intro: The exhibition opens to a room painted in the same deep blue as the original canvas. Elara places the artist’s notebook beside the finished portrait.
chapters.objective: Choose what the next exhibition will emphasize.

choices.label: Invite young restorers
choices.outcome: Elara creates a public conservation workshop, allowing visitors to learn how patience brings hidden histories to light.
choices.memoryHint: A conservation workshop welcomes new artists.

choices.label: Share the research archive
choices.outcome: The museum releases its annotated research and high-resolution scans so others can question and build on the discovery.
choices.memoryHint: The research archive becomes accessible.

chapters.title: The Third Layer
chapters.setting: A canvas with too many hands
chapters.intro: A routine scan of the gallery's newest acquisition reveals a third composition beneath the second: a rougher sketch, signed with the same gold mark. Elara is looking at a teacher, an apprentice, and a student in one frame.

echoes.elara_c1_a: Infrared showed you the first hidden face. This time the deeper layer is not a face but a pair of hands.
echoes.elara_c1_b: The frame once pointed you to an overlooked artist. The same frame builder's mark appears under the stretcher.

chapters.objective: Choose how to untangle the layers.

choices.label: Scan the entire collection
choices.outcome: Elara books the scanner for a week. Four more works reveal hidden layers, and a pattern emerges: the apprentice was completing other people's abandoned compositions.
choices.memoryHint: Hidden layers appear across the collection.

choices.label: Trace the teacher's pigments
choices.outcome: A pigment specialist identifies a green used by only one workshop. The teacher's hand is in three works the catalog credits to nobody at all.
choices.memoryHint: One workshop green links three works.

chapters.title: The Donor's Condition
chapters.setting: A lawyer in the conservation lab
chapters.intro: The donor's family asks that the hidden layer be covered again. They say the second face was a private grief, never meant for walls. The gallery's new scan is already scheduled for the reopening.

echoes.elara_c3_a: You showed both layers side by side. The family has seen the display and calls it an exposure.
echoes.elara_c3_b: You reattributed the catalog. The family accepts the scholarship and rejects the attention.

chapters.objective: Choose how to honor the donor and the evidence.

choices.label: Negotiate a rotating display
choices.outcome: Elara proposes a room that shows the hidden layer for one season and rests it for two. The family agrees, on condition that the grief is named in the label.
choices.memoryHint: The hidden layer rotates with a named grief.

choices.label: Publish the condition and evidence
choices.outcome: Elara writes an open account of the family's request and the gallery's obligation. The public debate is noisy; the family withdraws the demand but not the hurt.
choices.memoryHint: The donor's condition becomes public record.

chapters.title: The Apprentice's Room
chapters.setting: A storage room of unattributed work
chapters.intro: Behind the gallery, a room holds thirty unattributed studies. Two living families each claim the same hand. Elara can settle it with a label, or leave the room open to a slower kind of answer.

echoes.elara_c4_a: Your workshop taught visitors that patience reveals hidden work. Both families attended it.
echoes.elara_c4_b: Your research archive invited challenge. The challenge has arrived with two family trees.

chapters.objective: Choose how attribution moves forward.

choices.label: Invite both families to attribute
choices.outcome: Elara gives each family a wall and a label card. The room becomes two rooms in conversation. Neither claim is settled; both are visible, and visitors read them together.
choices.memoryHint: Two families share the attribution room.

choices.label: Use a community attribution panel
choices.outcome: Elara convenes conservators, descendants and local historians. The panel credits the workshop rather than a single hand — an answer that satisfies no one completely and holds.
choices.memoryHint: A panel credits the workshop, not one hand.

chapters.title: The Gallery of Hands
chapters.intro: The reopening is a week away. Elara can mount a show about one recovered genius, or a show about collaboration — the hands that finished, repaired, and sometimes erased each other's work. The walls are the same deep blue either way.

echoes.elara_c2_a: The shared cobalt once told you two canvases belonged together. The pigment is in five works now.
echoes.elara_c2_b: The registrar's photograph identified an overlooked apprentice. Her grandchildren are coming to the opening.

chapters.objective: Choose what the gallery will teach.

choices.label: Build the show around one artist
choices.outcome: The gallery gathers the apprentice's work into a single luminous room. Visitors leave knowing a name. The teacher and the student fade into footnotes, and Elara wonders if that is a kindness.
choices.memoryHint: One overlooked artist takes the spotlight.

choices.label: Build the show around many hands
choices.outcome: Each wall names three contributors: who began, who finished, who saved. Visitors argue about whether a painting can have a chorus. The apprentice's name is one voice among them, and no smaller for it.
choices.memoryHint: The exhibition credits many hands.

chapters.title: The Invoice Beside the Painting
chapters.intro:
The Blue Gallery is open. Its first season has brought invitations, complaints and a maintenance budget smaller than the opening budget. Cass places an invoice beside a reproduction of the painting. The caption acknowledges many kinds of work; the payment schedule has not caught up.

Elara begins describing what the exhibition changed. Cass asks her to describe what it cost. There is no anger in the question she can safely turn into a debate about art. There are hours, late payments and a technician who cannot keep donating them.

The gallery can commission a paid maintenance contract now, reducing the next exhibition, or publish a costed conservation plan and phase the work while suspending the most demanding loans. Both routes give up something visible. Elara looks at the bright opening-night photograph and notices who is outside its frame.
chapters.objective: Decide how the gallery pays for the care it publicly celebrates.

echoes.elara_c8_a: A single artist anchors the exhibition. Cass's invoice describes the many people whose work keeps that singular story on the wall.
echoes.elara_c8_b: The exhibition names many hands. Cass asks whether those hands will also appear in a funded maintenance plan.

choices.label: Fund a paid maintenance contract now
choices.outcome: Elara helps move money from the next exhibition into a contract with scheduled hours, material costs and a clear scope. The next opening is less ambitious. Cass negotiates two terms Elara would have called minor before seeing the invoice. They sign without turning the agreement into a story about generosity. A smaller gallery programme now rests on work someone can afford to do.
choices.memoryHint: Maintenance labor receives a funded contract rather than another acknowledgment.

choices.label: Publish a phased plan and reduce the loans
choices.outcome: The gallery publishes its care backlog and costs, returns the loans it cannot responsibly maintain, and funds the first stage of a paid conservation plan. Empty spaces interrupt the exhibition. Cass labels one of them with what care would require, then returns to the work already contracted. Visitors see a limit the opening concealed. Elara accepts a less flattering but more accurate room.
choices.memoryHint: The gallery makes its care limits visible and reduces unsupported commitments.

chapters.title: A Label She Does Not Write
chapters.setting: A working table in the blue room
chapters.intro:
The season's final wall text is about conservation itself. Elara has a polished draft in which every uncertainty arrives at exactly the right sentence. Cass reads it, smiles once, and asks what a colleague could change without asking Elara first.

On the table are notes from the people who prepared the room. Some contradict one another. One says the exhibition repaired an omission; another says it offered a new, more elegant way to hide the same hierarchy. Elara wants to answer both. Instead she asks what an honest final label should allow.

There is room for a signed conversation between contributors, or for a shorter institutional statement whose underlying decisions and revisions remain available. Neither arrangement will make disagreement disappear. The wall has enough space for either, but not for Elara to keep the final word by default.
chapters.objective: Choose how the gallery records disagreement about its own work.

echoes.elara_c9_a: The paid maintenance contract makes care a shared working arrangement. The final label can now be negotiated without asking people to donate more labor.
echoes.elara_c9_b: The visible gaps already acknowledge a limit. The final label needs to explain that limit without presenting restraint as a finished achievement.

choices.label: Publish a paid, signed contributors conversation
choices.outcome: The gallery pays contributors to edit a signed exchange, including disagreements that remain unresolved. Elara removes her concluding paragraph when the group asks. Cass's account ends on an unfinished task, not an image. Some visitors find the wall untidy. Others return to read a different voice. The painting stays in the same place; the explanation no longer stands in front of it.
choices.memoryHint: Contributors keep distinct, paid voices without an imposed final conclusion.

choices.label: Publish an accountable institutional statement
choices.outcome: Elara and the gallery team issue a short statement accepting responsibility for the decisions and funding limits. A nearby register preserves objections, revisions and named authors where permission is given. Cass approves the description of her work but does not endorse the whole exhibition. The statement records that distinction. Elara signs it as a custodian, not the owner of everyone's account.
choices.memoryHint: The institution owns its decisions and preserves dissent without implying endorsement.

title: Signals After Midnight
tagline: One midnight broadcast can change a city.
premise: A caller leaves a recorded message that predicts the next song exactly.

chapters.title: The Impossible Request
chapters.intro: At 12:07 a.m., Rowan receives an audio message announcing a song that the station has not yet queued. When the song begins, a second voice whispers the name of a bridge.
chapters.objective: Decide where to begin looking.

choices.label: Check the audio timestamp
choices.outcome: The recording predates the station’s schedule. Rowan finds evidence of a forgotten automated playlist service.
choices.memoryHint: The timestamp exposes an old scheduling system.

choices.label: Ask listeners about the bridge
choices.outcome: Three callers describe a bridge that no longer appears on transit maps. Rowan collects their stories without sharing private addresses.
choices.memoryHint: Listeners remember the missing bridge.

chapters.title: Static and Memory
chapters.intro: Old tapes in the radio archive reveal a series made by teenagers before the neighborhood station closed. The mysterious voice sounds like one of its hosts.
chapters.objective: Choose how to verify the voice.

choices.label: Restore the original tapes
choices.outcome: Rowan cleans the audio with the station engineer. A station identifier appears between the songs.
choices.memoryHint: Restored tapes reveal the old station identifier.

choices.label: Trace the broadcast license
choices.outcome: A public record identifies the youth radio project that once broadcast from the bridge district.
choices.memoryHint: A public record locates the youth project.

chapters.title: The Community Signal
chapters.intro: Rowan learns the strange requests were part of a time capsule, programmed by young broadcasters decades ago. Its final message has never aired.
chapters.objective: Choose a respectful way to share it.

choices.label: Contact the original creators
choices.outcome: Rowan locates two former producers and asks permission to broadcast their message. They offer context and a new introduction.
choices.memoryHint: Original creators approve the broadcast.

choices.label: Open a listening archive
choices.outcome: Rowan digitizes the recordings and invites listeners to contribute corrections, keeping personal content private.
choices.memoryHint: The station builds a listening archive.

chapters.title: One Last Song
chapters.intro: At midnight Rowan plays the newly restored recording, followed by songs chosen by the neighborhood that once lived around the bridge.
chapters.objective: Choose the future of the station.

choices.label: Start a monthly memory hour
choices.outcome: Rowan announces a monthly hour dedicated to people telling their own local histories. The first caller is already waiting.
choices.memoryHint: A monthly memory hour is born.

choices.label: Publish a neighborhood sound map
choices.outcome: The station publishes a consent-based sound map, connecting places with the voices that remember them.
choices.memoryHint: A neighborhood sound map goes live.

chapters.title: The Caller Returns
chapters.intro: The midnight request happens again — this time live. A caller with a young voice asks for a song the station has never played, then adds a name from the old bridge archive. Rowan has ninety seconds of airtime to decide what to do.

echoes.rowan_c1_a: The timestamp once exposed a forgotten playlist. This caller knows the old schedule by heart.
echoes.rowan_c1_b: You once collected bridge stories from listeners. The caller's name belongs to one of them.

chapters.objective: Choose how to handle the live call.

choices.label: Keep the caller on air
choices.outcome: Rowan lets the caller speak, with consent, and the voice describes a station that vanished before they were born. The line goes quiet at 12:11. The switchboard lights up.
choices.memoryHint: A live caller describes the lost station.

choices.label: Trace the line while playing the song
choices.outcome: The song buys Rowan time. The call routes through a community center that closed a decade ago, and the number belongs to a youth program that still meets in its basement.
choices.memoryHint: The call routes to a living youth program.

chapters.title: The Bridge Frequency
chapters.intro: A transmitter is still running beneath the old bridge, powered by a line nobody bills. The city wants it removed before inspection season. The last unplayed tape is still inside its housing, and the youth program says the frequency is theirs.

echoes.rowan_c3_a: The original producers trusted you with their final message. The program is asking for the same trust now.
echoes.rowan_c3_b: Your listening archive invited corrections. The transmitter is the correction no one expected.

chapters.objective: Decide what happens to the transmitter.

choices.label: Broadcast the final tape first
choices.outcome: Rowan airs the last recording with the program's permission and a clear introduction. The city inspector listens to the whole thing before writing the removal order, then grants a month's stay.
choices.memoryHint: The last tape earns the transmitter a month.

choices.label: Invite engineers to preserve it
choices.outcome: A volunteer engineer documents the transmitter and builds a low-power replica for the program. The original is retired with a plaque; the frequency stays alive in a new box.
choices.memoryHint: The transmitter is preserved in a replica.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Static
chapters.setting: A studio with the lights low
chapters.intro: The voice belongs to a former youth host, now in her fifties, who left the program after a public mistake she has never discussed. She agrees to meet, but not yet to be recorded. Rowan has one microphone and no deadline.

echoes.rowan_c4_a: Your memory hour promised people could tell their own histories. She has heard the promise.
echoes.rowan_c4_b: Your sound map connected places to voices. Hers is the voice of one of those places.

chapters.objective: Choose how to tell her story.

choices.label: Offer an unedited interview
choices.outcome: She speaks for two hours, including the part she has never said aloud. Rowan airs it with her approval and no cuts. The station receives its first complaint and its longest thank-you letter in years.
choices.memoryHint: An unedited interview airs with consent.

choices.label: Let her choose what airs
choices.outcome: She records three versions and picks the shortest. What remains is careful, incomplete, and entirely hers. Rowan learns that a story can be true without being whole.
choices.memoryHint: The host chooses her own version.

chapters.title: Signals After Midnight
chapters.setting: The booth at the end of the night
chapters.intro: The station offers Rowan a permanent slot: a weekly archive hour, fully funded, with a producer and a lawyer. The alternative is to keep the midnight mystery alive — unanswered calls, unlisted songs, a signal that belongs to whoever is listening.

echoes.rowan_c2_a: You restored the tapes and found the station identifier. The identifier is still in the archive, waiting.
echoes.rowan_c2_b: You traced the license to the bridge district. The district still has no station of its own.

chapters.objective: Choose what the midnight signal becomes.

choices.label: Take the weekly archive hour
choices.outcome: The archive hour becomes a fixture. Calls are screened, tapes are cataloged, and the mystery becomes a beloved institution. Some nights Rowan misses the static, and says so on air.
choices.memoryHint: The archive becomes a weekly institution.

choices.label: Keep the midnight signal open
choices.outcome: Rowan turns down the slot and keeps the line open once a month, unscreened. Some calls are nonsense. One is a station identifier nobody has heard in forty years, and he lets it play.
choices.memoryHint: The midnight line stays open.

chapters.title: The Morning After the Recording
chapters.setting: The studio, without a red light
chapters.intro:
Tamsin calls after a long conversation at the station. She has changed her mind about one passage and wants it removed before any further broadcast. Rowan knows exactly which passage: it is the one he had already imagined opening with.

There is no mystery in her request. The difficult part is his impulse to explain how well the passage would help listeners understand her. Tamsin waits while he notices that impulse. Outside the studio, an adult volunteer is updating the schedule; the blank slot is not an emergency.

Rowan can rebuild the programme around what she still wants to share, or leave the slot empty of her material and make a separate, clearly introduced programme about the archive's methods. Both options cost him an ending he liked. Neither entitles him to ask her to justify changing her mind.
chapters.objective: Respond to withdrawn permission without treating it as a creative obstacle.

echoes.rowan_c8_a: The weekly archive hour has a producer and a lawyer. Their schedule gives Rowan support, but no right to keep material its speaker has withdrawn.
echoes.rowan_c8_b: The midnight signal remains open. Rowan must still distinguish an invitation to speak from permission for every later use.

choices.label: Rebuild only from material she approves
choices.outcome: Rowan returns a revised sequence to Tamsin with the removed passage absent from both audio and promotion. The programme becomes less neatly resolved. She approves some of it and declines a suggested link. He leaves that gap alone. Before broadcast they agree on the uses covered by her approval, without describing her choice as bravery she now has to live up to.
choices.memoryHint: The programme is rebuilt around specific, current permission.

choices.label: Withdraw her material from this programme
choices.outcome: Rowan takes Tamsin's material out of the scheduled programme and offers to discuss future use only if she wishes. He fills the slot with an honest account of the station's archive practices, using no details that would identify her request. The episode gets fewer responses. Tamsin later sends a note about an unrelated song. He answers the question she actually asked.
choices.memoryHint: The station accepts losing an episode rather than turn refusal into content.

chapters.title: The Unbroadcast Ending
chapters.setting: A blank card beside the microphone
chapters.intro:
The station asks Rowan to write the rule he wants the next host to inherit. Tamsin agrees to discuss the wording without being quoted. They sit on the listener side of the desk. The microphone is not connected.

One proposal gives contributors a review window before each new use, with a practical way to withdraw approval. Another keeps sensitive personal recordings out of the reusable archive and allows only narrowly agreed broadcasts. The first needs sustained administration. The second means some programmes will exist only as a note that something once aired.

Rowan turns over a blank archive card. He once believed that every unfilled card represented a lost connection. Now he can imagine a person returning to the station because there is no recording waiting to speak for them. He asks which kind of promise the station can actually keep.
chapters.objective: Choose what the station owes people after the microphone switches off.

echoes.rowan_c9_a: The rebuilt programme has precise permission for its current use. The next host needs a process that will not mistake that approval for an unlimited license.
echoes.rowan_c9_b: A withdrawn programme has left a real gap in the schedule. The archive policy must allow a gap to remain a legitimate outcome.

choices.label: Fund review and withdrawal before reuse
choices.outcome: The station assigns paid time to contributor review, permission records and withdrawal requests before reuse. Repeats become harder to schedule. Rowan cancels a favorite compilation when one approval cannot be renewed. Tamsin reads the process and asks for a simpler contact route; he changes it. The final card names the programme, its permitted uses and the person responsible for asking again.
choices.memoryHint: Future reuse requires a funded review and withdrawal process.

choices.label: Keep sensitive recordings out of the reusable archive
choices.outcome: The station limits sensitive personal material to specifically agreed broadcasts and keeps a minimal programme record rather than reusable audio. Some history survives only in descriptions its speakers approve. Rowan dislikes the empty shelf more than he expected, but stops calling it a failure. On the next quiet evening, Tamsin comes by for tea. No one reaches for a microphone.
choices.memoryHint: Sensitive recordings stay outside a reusable archive unless separately agreed.

title: The Map Between Stars
tagline: Chart the constellation that should not exist.
premise: Seraphine notices a constellation that appears only in forgotten sketches.

chapters.title: The Ninth Pattern
chapters.intro: Seraphine discovers a constellation drawn in three centuries of unrelated diaries, each with an identical missing star. The modern sky contains no matching pattern.
chapters.objective: Choose your first line of inquiry.

choices.label: Map the drawings by date
choices.outcome: A pattern emerges in the dates: each sketch coincides with a rare atmospheric halo over the valley.
choices.memoryHint: The drawings align with unusual sky conditions.

choices.label: Examine the observatory glass
choices.outcome: A retired lens creates a blue ghost reflection that mimics part of the constellation. One missing star remains unexplained.
choices.memoryHint: An old lens explains most, but not all, of the pattern.

chapters.title: The Glass Meridian
chapters.intro: A storm clears above an abandoned observatory. Seraphine finds its dome aligned to the northern ridge rather than true north.
chapters.objective: Choose a careful observation.

choices.label: Measure the dome alignment
choices.outcome: A survey shows the old alignment follows the path of a once-visible comet in the observatory’s founding year.
choices.memoryHint: The dome points to an old comet path.

choices.label: Study the founder’s journal
choices.outcome: The founder described the pattern as a poetic map of migrating lanterns, not a literal star chart.
choices.memoryHint: The founder called the constellation a poetic map.

chapters.title: A Constellation of Letters
chapters.intro: The diagrams contain tiny marginal marks that correspond to letters in a lost astronomical society’s alphabet. They form directions to a cabinet beneath the dome.
chapters.objective: Choose how to open the cabinet.

choices.label: Ask the archive curator
choices.outcome: The curator helps safely open the cabinet and inventories a collection of letters and weather records.
choices.memoryHint: The cabinet opens under archive supervision.

choices.label: Decipher the final symbol
choices.outcome: Seraphine decodes the final mark as a date of remembrance rather than a celestial coordinate.
choices.memoryHint: The final symbol marks a day of remembrance.

chapters.title: Where the Light Lands
chapters.setting: A new map for the night
chapters.intro: The so-called lost star was a communal symbol used by generations of stargazers to remember people they could no longer see. Seraphine opens the dome to visitors.
chapters.objective: Choose what the observatory will share.

choices.label: Host a night of stories
choices.outcome: Visitors tell skyward stories while Seraphine identifies real stars and honors the legends as legends.
choices.memoryHint: An observatory story night brings the community together.

choices.label: Create an annotated star atlas
choices.outcome: Seraphine publishes two maps side by side: measured sky positions and the imaginative atlas that inspired the search.
choices.memoryHint: An atlas separates science from storytelling.

chapters.title: The Second Missing Star
chapters.setting: A dome that opens on schedule
chapters.intro: A year after the first exhibition, a new sketch arrives in the post: the same constellation, drawn by a child, with a different star missing. Seraphine checks the real sky twice. The pattern is not astronomy. It is becoming a language.

echoes.seraphine_c1_a: You once mapped the drawings by their dates. This one is undated, and its paper is new.
echoes.seraphine_c1_b: You let an old lens explain most of the pattern. The child's missing star sits exactly where the lens could not reach.

chapters.objective: Decide how to study the new drawing.

choices.label: Ask the child's family
choices.outcome: The drawing was made at a bedside, for someone who could not go outside. The missing star was left blank on purpose, the child explains, because that person is not gone yet.
choices.memoryHint: A child's drawing leaves a star for the living.

choices.label: Compare it with the older sketches
choices.outcome: Every generation leaves out a different star, and the omitted stars trace a slow drift across the sky. Seraphine realizes the constellation has been edited, carefully, for three hundred years.
choices.memoryHint: Each generation edits the constellation.

chapters.title: The Founder's Granddaughter
chapters.intro: The founder's granddaughter arrives with a box of letters and a request. She wants the observatory's official history to stop calling the constellation 'a poetic error', a phrase her grandfather fought against for forty years.

echoes.seraphine_c3_a: You opened the cabinet under archive supervision. The granddaughter asks for the same care with her family's name.
echoes.seraphine_c3_b: You read the final symbol as a date of remembrance. She has brought the letters that prove you right.

chapters.objective: Choose how the record is corrected.

choices.label: Rewrite the label with her
choices.outcome: Seraphine and the granddaughter draft a new interpretation together: a memorial practice, not a mistake. The old phrase stays visible, struck through rather than erased. Both of them sign the note.
choices.memoryHint: The label is rewritten with the family.

choices.label: Publish her letters as a source
choices.outcome: The observatory digitizes the letters with her permission and publishes them as primary sources. Historians disagree in print. The family's account is at last impossible to overlook.
choices.memoryHint: The family's letters become public sources.

chapters.title: The Sky in the Archive
chapters.setting: A reading room of weather diaries
chapters.intro: A university offers to buy the sketch collection and keep it in climate-controlled storage two hundred miles away. The observatory can accept the money and the preservation, or keep the drawings where the valley can still walk in and see them.

echoes.seraphine_c4_a: Your story nights filled the dome with people who had never read a chart. The collection is now theirs as much as yours.
echoes.seraphine_c4_b: Your twin atlas put measurement beside imagination. The university wants only the imagination, cataloged.

chapters.objective: Decide where the drawings live.

choices.label: Accept the conservation partnership
choices.outcome: The originals travel to the university; high-resolution facsimiles stay in the dome. Seraphine insists the loan agreement includes a local reading day each year, and the first one is standing room only.
choices.memoryHint: The originals travel, the copies stay.

choices.label: Keep the collection in the valley
choices.outcome: Seraphine turns down the sale and raises the money in small donations instead. The storage is imperfect and the drawings are loved. Every envelope has a repair she can name.
choices.memoryHint: The drawings stay in the valley.

chapters.title: The Ninth Star
chapters.setting: The dome, open to the valley
chapters.intro: The observatory can now advertise itself as the place where the lost constellation was solved, or as the place where generations kept a promise to remember each other. The second story is harder to market and harder to lose.

echoes.seraphine_c2_a: The dome was aligned to a comet, not to true north. Seraphine has stopped correcting that, and started explaining it.
echoes.seraphine_c2_b: The founder called the pattern a poetic map. The whole valley is about to be told what he meant.

chapters.objective: Choose the observatory's public identity.

choices.label: Market the solved mystery
choices.outcome: Visitor numbers triple. The gift shop sells constellation prints with the missing star blank, as a joke that lands differently for every family. Seraphine answers the same three questions all summer and never once regrets the roof.
choices.memoryHint: The solved mystery draws a crowd.

choices.label: Keep it a place of remembrance
choices.outcome: The observatory advertises one line: 'Bring a name.' People come at dusk and leave with a star they chose themselves. Seraphine keeps a private log of the ones who come back, and there are many.
choices.memoryHint: The dome becomes a place to bring names.

title: The Glass Network
tagline: Protect a future no algorithm can predict.
premise: A city prediction network flags a peaceful neighborhood as a hazard.

chapters.title: The False Alarm
chapters.setting: The wrong side of the glass
chapters.intro: Kai’s city safety dashboard marks a quiet block as unusually dangerous despite no matching reports from residents. An opaque automated score has overridden the local team.
chapters.objective: Choose a fair first step.

choices.label: Audit the input data
choices.outcome: A duplicated data feed exaggerates nighttime foot traffic. Kai documents the error before changing any alert level.
choices.memoryHint: A duplicated sensor feed is identified.

choices.label: Ask neighborhood stewards
choices.outcome: Residents describe a night market mistaken for an emergency gathering. Kai records their account with consent.
choices.memoryHint: The alert confused a thriving market with risk.

chapters.title: A Street With No Number
chapters.setting: Who was left off the map
chapters.intro: The city network routes maintenance workers around an entire block. Kai discovers that public access ramps disappeared in a recent mapping update.
chapters.objective: Choose how to restore access.

choices.label: Recheck the public maps
choices.outcome: Kai compares historic and current accessibility maps, finding an incorrect coordinate transformation.
choices.memoryHint: A mapping error hid accessible routes.

choices.label: Walk the route with volunteers
choices.outcome: The team verifies ramp locations with accessibility advocates and reports each obstacle precisely.
choices.memoryHint: Volunteers create a verified accessible route.

chapters.title: The Human Override
chapters.setting: A decision no score should make
chapters.intro: City officials request an instant safety rating for the neighborhood. Kai argues for a human review that includes uncertainty and community input.
chapters.objective: Choose a transparent approach.

choices.label: Publish a plain-language audit
choices.outcome: Kai shares the verified error and how it was corrected, without revealing anyone’s personal data.
choices.memoryHint: The community receives a transparent audit.

choices.label: Create a review panel
choices.outcome: Kai sets up a resident-led review before future high-impact alerts can affect services.
choices.memoryHint: A human review panel protects future decisions.

chapters.title: A City That Listens
chapters.intro: The repaired map finally shows the market, the ramps, and the people who keep the block alive. Kai returns to the street at dusk as the music begins.
chapters.objective: Choose the next improvement.

choices.label: Launch an error-report channel
choices.outcome: Citizens can now flag incorrect city data and see when each correction is verified.
choices.memoryHint: An accountable error-report channel is established.

choices.label: Publish an accessibility guide
choices.outcome: Kai’s team creates a free neighborhood guide developed with local volunteers.
choices.memoryHint: Residents get a verified accessibility guide.

chapters.title: The Score Returns
chapters.setting: A dashboard that disagrees with itself
chapters.intro: Six months after the review panel, the automated score flags the same block again — with a methodology nobody on the panel recognizes. The vendor calls it an improvement. Kai calls it a second unopened box.

echoes.kai_c1_a: You found a duplicated feed once. This model cites that same feed as its training source.
echoes.kai_c1_b: You recorded residents' accounts with consent. Those records are the only evidence the new model never saw.

chapters.objective: Choose how to contest the new score.

choices.label: Request the model's training data
choices.outcome: The vendor refuses, citing trade secrets. Kai publishes the refusal verbatim and the panel votes to suspend the score until it can be explained. The alarm stays off for a week.
choices.memoryHint: The unexplained score is suspended.

choices.label: Run a parallel human review
choices.outcome: Kai assigns two residents and one auditor to re-score the block by hand. Their result is eleven points lower than the model's. The gap becomes the agenda for the next hearing.
choices.memoryHint: A human review scores eleven points lower.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Block
chapters.setting: A street the model learned to avoid
chapters.intro: Maintenance crews still skip a block along the canal, months after the ramp data was corrected. Kai discovers the old score was baked into a routing contract that nobody has reopened. The people on the block have stopped expecting the truck.

echoes.kai_c3_a: You published a plain-language audit. That audit is now the only document proving the contract is obsolete.
echoes.kai_c3_b: Your review panel was built for alerts. It has no power over contracts, which is exactly why this happened.

chapters.objective: Decide how to reopen the route.

choices.label: Rebid the routing contract
choices.outcome: Kai spends a month writing accessibility requirements into the new contract. The process is slow, public, and dull. On the first morning the truck returns, someone on the block puts a chair out on the pavement.
choices.memoryHint: The new contract includes access requirements.

choices.label: Run an interim volunteer route
choices.outcome: Kai organizes a volunteer service while the contract is rewritten. It works, and it is fragile, and the block now knows exactly what the city owes them. The chair stays out every Tuesday.
choices.memoryHint: A volunteer route fills the gap.

chapters.title: The Wrong Kind of Help
chapters.setting: A laptop with too much access
chapters.intro: A young engineer on Kai's team offers to fix the vendor's model directly. She has found a way in, and she is certain she would only change the one skewed variable. Kai remembers what he promised about reckless hacking.

echoes.kai_c4_a: You built an error-report channel so citizens could challenge the data openly. Quietly editing a vendor's model is the opposite door.
echoes.kai_c4_b: Your accessibility guide won trust on the block. Trust is the thing that editing without permission would spend.

chapters.objective: Choose a response to the offer.

choices.label: Turn the find into a disclosure
choices.outcome: Kai guides her to write a security disclosure with a deadline and a public record. The vendor patches the flaw, grudgingly, and credits her in a changelog nobody reads but auditors.
choices.memoryHint: The flaw becomes a public disclosure.

choices.label: Build a sanctioned test harness
choices.outcome: Kai secures permission for a supervised test environment. She reproduces the skew with witnesses and documents. The fix takes three weeks longer and survives appeal, which the quiet edit would not have.
choices.memoryHint: A supervised harness proves the skew.

chapters.title: A City That Answers
chapters.setting: The panel room, one year on
chapters.intro: The city offers Kai a permanent office with a budget and a title. The other option is to stay a liaison with no title, still walking the block on Tuesdays, still the person residents call first. Both are real power, and only one scales.

echoes.kai_c2_a: A mapping error once erased the ramps. The new office would hold the map, and the key to every correction.
echoes.kai_c2_b: Volunteers verified the accessible route street by street. That method does not fit neatly into an org chart.

chapters.objective: Choose where Kai's work goes next.

choices.label: Take the office
choices.outcome: Kai accepts, and his first act is to publish the org chart with the panel's authority drawn above his own. He misses the Tuesday walks. On the second week, he starts taking them anyway, on the record.
choices.memoryHint: Kai takes office and keeps walking.

choices.label: Stay the liaison
choices.outcome: Kai declines and keeps the block, the calls, and the awkward seat at every meeting. When the next model arrives, the people who live on the street are in the room before the vendor finishes the pitch.
choices.memoryHint: Kai stays where residents can reach him.

title: Tomorrow’s Table
tagline: Save a tiny café with a thousand stories.
premise: Luna discovers her grandmother’s recipe notebook tucked into a piano.

chapters.title: The Recipe in the Piano
chapters.intro: Luna discovers a notebook between the keys of her grandmother’s piano. Its last recipe is incomplete, and the café’s lease renewal is approaching.
chapters.objective: Decide where to start.

choices.label: Bake the first draft
choices.outcome: The bread smells wonderful but collapses when sliced. Luna writes down what went wrong instead of pretending it is perfect.
choices.memoryHint: The first loaf teaches Luna what is missing.

choices.label: Ask longtime regulars
choices.outcome: A retired neighbor remembers the missing ingredient as something brought from the Saturday market.
choices.memoryHint: A longtime neighbor recalls a market clue.

chapters.title: A Table for Strangers
chapters.intro: A slow afternoon turns into an unexpected gathering when a lost sketchbook is returned to the café. On its first page is a drawing of the old storefront.
chapters.objective: Choose how to bring people together.

choices.label: Host an open sketch evening
choices.outcome: The café fills with neighbors drawing their favorite corners of the district. Luna pins their pictures on a welcoming wall.
choices.memoryHint: An open sketch evening makes new connections.

choices.label: Create a recipe exchange
choices.outcome: Regulars share simple family recipes and the memories they choose to tell, with no pressure to reveal more.
choices.memoryHint: The café begins a community recipe exchange.

chapters.title: The Saturday Market
chapters.intro: Luna can afford either a new sign or a weekend tasting table. Her friends offer help, but she wants a plan she can sustain.
chapters.objective: Choose how to reach new guests.

choices.label: Run a small tasting table
choices.outcome: Luna prepares a limited batch and lets people choose what to pay. The honest response helps her refine the final recipe.
choices.memoryHint: A modest tasting table attracts curious neighbors.

choices.label: Redesign the storefront menu
choices.outcome: Luna writes a clear, inviting menu and photographs the food in morning light. More passersby stop to look.
choices.memoryHint: A simple menu makes the café easier to discover.

chapters.title: Tomorrow’s Table
chapters.intro: On the morning of the lease meeting, the café is full of familiar faces and first-time visitors. Luna brings the completed recipe notebook to the counter.
chapters.objective: Choose how the café will grow.

choices.label: Keep a community table
choices.outcome: Luna reserves one large table for neighbors who want to meet, play a game, or simply share quiet company.
choices.memoryHint: A community table becomes the café’s heart.

choices.label: Publish the café’s little book
choices.outcome: Luna publishes a tiny booklet of recipes and neighborhood sketches, crediting everyone who contributed.
choices.memoryHint: The café’s first story booklet finds its readers.

chapters.title: The Notebook's Last Page
chapters.intro: The final page of the notebook is a list of names, not a recipe. Fourteen people, each beside a dish Luna has never served. Her grandmother's handwriting gets larger and shakier toward the bottom of the page.

echoes.luna_c1_a: You wrote down what went wrong with the first loaf. The last page is also a record of what went wrong, in a different way.
echoes.luna_c1_b: A neighbor once recalled a market clue. Three of these names belong to people who still shop there.

chapters.objective: Decide what to do with the list.

choices.label: Cook the list, one name a week
choices.outcome: Luna puts one name on the menu each Sunday and tells the story she has, marking what she does not know. Four of the fourteen families come in. Two of them cry, gently, over soup.
choices.memoryHint: The list becomes a weekly menu of names.

choices.label: Ask the families first
choices.outcome: Luna writes to each family and asks what, if anything, they would like remembered. Six reply. The menu that emerges is smaller, stranger, and entirely theirs.
choices.memoryHint: Families choose what is remembered.

chapters.title: The Rent Notice
chapters.intro: The building's new owner offers Luna a five-year lease — at a rent that requires the café to become something faster and louder. The neighborhood table would not survive it. Luna has one month to answer.

echoes.luna_c3_a: You once let people choose what to pay. The new owner calls that a pricing error.
echoes.luna_c3_b: You rebuilt the menu to be discoverable. Now the owner wants the whole room to be discoverable from the street.

chapters.objective: Choose how to answer the lease.

choices.label: Negotiate a smaller café
choices.outcome: Luna gives up the back room and keeps the front. Fewer tables, the same community table, and a lease she can carry. The back room becomes a bakery that pays rent of its own.
choices.memoryHint: A smaller café survives the lease.

choices.label: Rally the regulars to buy in
choices.outcome: Forty regulars put in small amounts, and the café becomes partly theirs. The meetings are long and the coffee is free. Nobody agrees on the paint, and everybody comes to the vote.
choices.memoryHint: The regulars become part-owners.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Left
chapters.intro: A regular who moved away returns for one afternoon with her daughter, who has never seen the café. She asks Luna not to mention a difficult year she spent here. The daughter asks why everyone knows her mother's name.

echoes.luna_c4_a: Your community table was built for people who want to meet. This table needs to hold two different kinds of silence.
echoes.luna_c4_b: Your little book credited everyone who contributed. She is in it, under a name she now uses differently.

chapters.objective: Choose how to hold both requests.

choices.label: Follow her lead
choices.outcome: Luna greets her by her new name and lets her set the story. The daughter hears only what her mother chooses to tell, and the afternoon stays light. The book stays on the shelf, closed.
choices.memoryHint: The guest sets the story.

choices.label: Ask her what the book should say
choices.outcome: Luna offers to amend the booklet's entry. She reads it twice, changes one line, and leaves it otherwise. 'That year happened,' she says. 'It just isn't the whole of me.'
choices.memoryHint: The booklet is amended with consent.

chapters.title: A Table for Tomorrow
chapters.intro: The café has survived its first hard year. Luna can franchise the recipe and the name, or keep one room on one street and let it stay small. The notebook sits open on the counter, still unfinished, because she has started adding pages of her own.

echoes.luna_c2_a: Your sketch wall once filled with your neighbors' favorite corners. A franchise would need walls that look the same everywhere.
echoes.luna_c2_b: The recipe exchange taught you that a dish carries a person. Scaling it would mean deciding which people get carried.

chapters.objective: Choose what the café becomes.

choices.label: Franchise carefully
choices.outcome: Luna opens two more rooms, each with a local recipe page and a community table of its own. The bread is consistent. The arguments at the tables are not, and that is the part she protects.
choices.memoryHint: Three cafés, three local recipe pages.

choices.label: Keep one room
choices.outcome: Luna stays. The café stays small enough that she knows who is missing on a given Tuesday. She writes the last page of the notebook herself — a shopping list, and a note to whoever finds it next.
choices.memoryHint: The café stays small and known.

title: The Forgotten Station
tagline: Board the train that never reached the map.
premise: A century-old ticket points to a station erased from every timetable.

chapters.title: Ticket to Nowhere
chapters.intro: Dimitri finds a ticket stamped for Saint Orin Station, a place that appears on no railway map. The ticket bears a date one day after the line was supposedly closed.
chapters.objective: Choose a source to trust first.

choices.label: Examine the ticket press
choices.outcome: The perforation matches a rarely used municipal rail service rather than the passenger line.
choices.memoryHint: The ticket belongs to a forgotten service route.

choices.label: Search city newspapers
choices.outcome: A brief notice mentions a special train for a town festival, but the destination name was omitted from later archives.
choices.memoryHint: A newspaper mentions an unlisted festival train.

chapters.title: The Last Conductor
chapters.intro: At a small railway museum, Dimitri finds a conductor’s suitcase containing a route sketch and a photograph of a platform beside a clock tower.
chapters.objective: Choose how to read the clues.

choices.label: Trace the clock tower
choices.outcome: Historic photographs show the tower at a relocated workers’ district. Dimitri locates the original platform foundation.
choices.memoryHint: The clock tower leads to the old platform.

choices.label: Compare the route sketch
choices.outcome: Dimitri overlays the sketch on a modern map and finds a short line buried beneath a public garden.
choices.memoryHint: The old route crosses a modern garden.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Stop
chapters.intro: The station was a temporary stop built by factory workers, never listed in the official passenger timetable. Local families still have photographs of its opening day.
chapters.objective: Choose how to protect their stories.

choices.label: Record consented oral histories
choices.outcome: Dimitri interviews willing descendants and asks them to review every quotation before publication.
choices.memoryHint: The families approve their own oral histories.

choices.label: Catalog the family photographs
choices.outcome: The museum digitizes photographs with credited owners and careful uncertainty labels.
choices.memoryHint: The museum preserves a family-led photo archive.

chapters.title: The Return Journey
chapters.intro: An exhibition opens beside the public garden where trains once stopped. Dimitri stands in the footprint of the old platform and unfolds the mysterious ticket.
chapters.objective: Choose the story’s final form.

choices.label: Make a walking history route
choices.outcome: Dimitri develops an accessible walking route with residents, making the old station visible without inventing new history.
choices.memoryHint: A walking route restores the station to local memory.

choices.label: Write the station chronicle
choices.outcome: Dimitri completes a short, well-sourced local chronicle, marking every uncertainty for future researchers.
choices.memoryHint: The forgotten station gains a careful chronicle.

chapters.title: The Route Beneath the Garden
chapters.setting: A public garden at first light
chapters.intro: Ground-penetrating radar confirms a short stretch of track under the garden's east lawn. The city wants to build a drainage channel there. Dimitri has a survey, a witness, and forty years of archived timetables that do not mention the line.

echoes.dimitri_c1_a: You traced the ticket to a forgotten service. The service ran exactly here, and the ticket's date is now evidence.
echoes.dimitri_c1_b: A newspaper once mentioned an unlisted festival train. The festival's route is on the survey in front of you.

chapters.objective: Decide how the track enters the argument.

choices.label: Submit the survey as heritage evidence
choices.outcome: Dimitri files the radar and the timetable gap together, with every uncertainty marked. The channel is rerouted by nine meters at a cost the city calls acceptable. The track stays buried.
choices.memoryHint: The drainage channel is rerouted.

choices.label: Open the lawn to a public dig
choices.outcome: Dimitri organizes a supervised weekend excavation with an archaeologist. Two hundred people queue to brush soil off a rail. What they find is a bolt, a coin, and a story that now has witnesses.
choices.memoryHint: A public dig uncovers a rail and a story.

chapters.title: The Photographer's Heir
chapters.intro: The platform photograph turns out to be one of six, taken by a factory worker who died before the station was erased from the maps. Her grandson offers the negatives to Dimitri on one condition: the exhibition must not call her 'an amateur'.
