choices.outcome: Ewan describes a night shift with workers arriving after the public entrances closed. He gives Vera a receipt from a small staff canteen. It identifies the passage by its everyday use, not by the dramatic name she had begun to imagine.
choices.memoryHint: Ewan describes a night shift with workers arriving after the public entrances closed.

echoes.vera_c1_a: Earlier in your journey: Vera finds that each edition inherits the same narrow strip of blank paper.
echoes.vera_c1_b: Earlier in your journey: The punch belongs to a staff shuttle rather than an ordinary passenger service.

chapters.title: The Name on the Cup
chapters.intro: A cup in the station collection bears a name missing from the staff list. Ewan recognizes it and asks for a day before saying more. Vera has enough material to request another archive search, but not enough to decide why the name disappeared. A pencilled menu on the back of the receipt gives her another way into the room's history without making him answer immediately.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to search the canteen supply records or wait for Ewan's account.

choices.label: Search the canteen supply records
choices.outcome: The supply book records meals for an additional crew during a long shutdown. Vera can show that the cup belonged in a working canteen, even without identifying its owner. Ewan notices that she has not used his hesitation as evidence against him.
choices.memoryHint: The supply book records meals for an additional crew during a long shutdown.

choices.label: Wait for Ewan's account
choices.outcome: The next afternoon Ewan returns with a photograph of adult night workers. He names the cup's owner as a colleague who organized their journeys home. He agrees to describe the service but asks that the photograph remain out of publicity.
choices.memoryHint: The next afternoon Ewan returns with a photograph of adult night workers.

echoes.vera_c2_a: Earlier in your journey: An approved inspection leads to a narrow observation window overlooking a disconnected bay.
echoes.vera_c2_b: Earlier in your journey: Ewan describes a night shift with workers arriving after the public entrances closed.

chapters.title: A Train for the Unlisted
chapters.intro: The missing departure was a staff shuttle, quietly omitted when a temporary arrangement became permanent. The bay outlived the service; the blank minute outlived the bay. Vera can explain much of the ticket, though not who recently sent it. The station asks for an account before reopening the old waiting room to visitors. Ewan wants the workers to appear as people with jobs, not the cast of a ghost story.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to build an exhibit around the workers or publish the timetable investigation.

choices.label: Build an exhibit around the workers
choices.outcome: Vera makes the shuttle's practical purpose the centre of the account. Contributors approve the details they share. The missing minute remains on a small facsimile timetable, beside names and work rather than an invented haunting. The sender is still unknown.
choices.memoryHint: Vera makes the shuttle's practical purpose the centre of the account.

choices.label: Publish the timetable investigation
choices.outcome: Vera explains the paper trail and labels the gaps that remain. Ewan's account appears only in the form he approved. Readers can follow how the mystery was reduced, rather than being asked to admire an explanation that knows more than its evidence.
choices.memoryHint: Vera explains the paper trail and labels the gaps that remain.

echoes.vera_c3_a: Earlier in your journey: The supply book records meals for an additional crew during a long shutdown.
echoes.vera_c3_b: Earlier in your journey: The next afternoon Ewan returns with a photograph of adult night workers.

chapters.title: A Return Ticket
chapters.intro: A second ticket reaches Vera with a note: RETURN, SAME MINUTE. The closed bay is still disconnected. On its reverse is a pattern of tiny punctures, different from the staff punch. Someone knows her investigation well enough to answer it. Vera can compare the paper or ask the contributor group whether the note means anything to them; neither option requires pretending that a train has returned.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to compare the paper and punctures or invite the contributors to read it.

choices.label: Compare the paper and punctures
choices.outcome: Vera identifies a modern reproduction stock and traces the punctures to the museum's demonstration punch. The ticket is a reply made from an old vocabulary. She feels a brief, unreasonable disappointment before noticing how carefully its sender studied the original. Decoding the demonstration pattern gives them a location inside the station.
choices.memoryHint: Vera identifies a modern reproduction stock and traces the punctures to the museum's demonstration punch.

choices.label: Invite the contributors to read it
choices.outcome: An adult former worker recognizes the pattern as a canteen game used during late shifts. With permission, she explains how the marks encode a location inside the station. Vera learns something the print records could never have supplied.
choices.memoryHint: An adult former worker recognizes the pattern as a canteen game used during late shifts.

echoes.vera_c4_a: Earlier in your journey: Vera makes the shuttle's practical purpose the centre of the account.
echoes.vera_c4_b: Earlier in your journey: Vera explains the paper trail and labels the gaps that remain.

chapters.title: The Last Connection
chapters.intro: The encoded location contains letters from workers who could no longer use the shuttle. Some are practical complaints; one describes missing a final visit to an adult sibling. A contributor asks Vera not to make that letter the emotional centre of the collection. The station will fund either a public reading or a private contributor session first. There is time for both eventually, but the first event will set expectations.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to start with a contributor session or start with a carefully limited public reading.

choices.label: Start with a contributor session
choices.outcome: The people connected to the service read the letters together and choose what can travel beyond the room. Several passages remain private. Vera's public talk becomes less dramatic and more accurate, and a contributor volunteers a different letter she had not known existed.
choices.memoryHint: The people connected to the service read the letters together and choose what can travel beyond the room.

choices.label: Start with a carefully limited public reading
choices.outcome: Vera prepares the event from passages explicitly approved for public use and states what has been withheld. The reading brings new witnesses forward, but contributors must answer more questions afterward. She budgets staff time to share that work.
choices.memoryHint: Vera prepares the event from passages explicitly approved for public use and states what has been withheld.

echoes.vera_c5_a: Earlier in your journey: Vera identifies a modern reproduction stock and traces the punctures to the museum's demonstration punch.
echoes.vera_c5_b: Earlier in your journey: An adult former worker recognizes the pattern as a canteen game used during late shifts.

chapters.title: Her Own Correction
chapters.intro: The recent sender is Ewan. He wanted Vera to find the letters without making his request another story about a reluctant witness. She is relieved, then angry that he tested her. He points to the correction she keeps in her coat and asks whether she has ever contacted the colleague whose timetable she dismissed. Vera can make that contact privately or place a clear correction in the published account.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to contact the colleague first or correct the published account first.

choices.label: Contact the colleague first
choices.outcome: Vera writes without asking for forgiveness or an interview. The colleague answers only the factual question about the old route. Vera accepts the limited reply and revises her notes. Repair begins with a smaller conversation than the one she had rehearsed.
choices.memoryHint: Vera writes without asking for forgiveness or an interview.

choices.label: Correct the published account first
choices.outcome: Vera adds a visible correction explaining whose timetable she dismissed and why that mattered, after confirming what may be named. She does not turn the correction into a defence of her intentions. Ewan reads it and stops calling her investigation a test.
choices.memoryHint: Vera adds a visible correction explaining whose timetable she dismissed and why that mattered, after confirming what may be named.

echoes.vera_c6_a: Earlier in your journey: The people connected to the service read the letters together and choose what can travel beyond the room.
echoes.vera_c6_b: Earlier in your journey: Vera prepares the event from passages explicitly approved for public use and states what has been withheld.

chapters.title: The Minute They Keep
chapters.intro: The old waiting room is ready. One proposal turns it into a regular public story room. Another reserves part of its opening time for former staff and their guests, keeping a quieter use alongside the exhibition. Neither can bring the shuttle back. Vera finally understands that the missing minute is not an invitation to make every private journey public. It is a place the station can choose to leave people.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to open a public story room or keep a quieter room within the station.

choices.label: Open a public story room
choices.outcome: The station creates a staffed room where approved accounts can be heard and corrected. Vera leads the first session, then gives the next one to a contributor. A visitor asks what time the ghost train leaves. She smiles and tells him about the workers instead.
choices.memoryHint: The station creates a staffed room where approved accounts can be heard and corrected.

choices.label: Keep a quieter room within the station
choices.outcome: The exhibition remains modest, with protected hours for contributors and guests. Some visitors object to a room they cannot always enter. Vera explains its purpose without apologizing for the boundary. At 17:09, Ewan makes coffee, and nobody has to become an exhibit.
choices.memoryHint: The exhibition remains modest, with protected hours for contributors and guests.

echoes.vera_c7_a: Earlier in your journey: Vera writes without asking for forgiveness or an interview.
echoes.vera_c7_b: Earlier in your journey: Vera adds a visible correction explaining whose timetable she dismissed and why that mattered, after confirming what may be named.

title: Glass Below the Harbor
tagline: A photograph can reveal a place and still miss its story.
premise: Look at the empty square in this mosaic. Yesterday it was filled in. Either the harbor moved, or my photograph is leaving something out.

chapters.title: The Empty Square
chapters.intro: Two photographs of an underwater mosaic disagree. A dark square in yesterday's image glows pale in today's, though the gallery log records no restoration work. Daria and Leena compare the images from a dry observation room. The discrepancy could come from the water, the glass or their assumptions. Daria leaves her usual dramatic caption unwritten and asks which part of the image they should test first.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to compare the shooting positions or compare the light conditions.

choices.label: Compare the shooting positions
choices.outcome: The camera positions differ by less than a step, enough to move a window reflection across the mosaic. Daria marks the reflection and keeps both images. The pale square remains unexplained, but one seductive version of the mystery can be set aside.
choices.memoryHint: The camera positions differ by less than a step, enough to move a window reflection across the mosaic.

choices.label: Compare the light conditions
choices.outcome: Leena matches the images to the gallery's lighting log. One light was off during the earlier exposure. Daria makes a new test series rather than choosing the photograph that best supports her first impression.
choices.memoryHint: Leena matches the images to the gallery's lighting log.

chapters.title: The Line in the Water
chapters.setting: A map of the old harbor
chapters.intro: A survey plan places a former waterline through the mosaic. Leena remembers a painted stripe in the public hall; Daria remembers a long blue wall. Neither memory identifies the missing square. The survey team can supply older images or undertake a limited exterior inspection. Daria has to decide what evidence is worth asking others to gather, rather than treating every unanswered question as a reason to send someone back.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to request the older image sequence or request an authorized exterior survey.

choices.label: Request the older image sequence
choices.outcome: The sequence shows repairs accumulated across several decades. A replacement panel is slightly raised, catching light differently from its neighbors. Daria can see a history of maintenance where she had imagined a single act of disappearance.
choices.memoryHint: The sequence shows repairs accumulated across several decades.

choices.label: Request an authorized exterior survey
choices.outcome: The qualified survey team documents deposits along the raised panel and provides a cautious account of visibility limits. The dark square may conceal an inscription. Daria publishes none of the early guesses as a discovery.
choices.memoryHint: The qualified survey team documents deposits along the raised panel and provides a cautious account of visibility limits.

echoes.daria_c1_a: Earlier in your journey: The camera positions differ by less than a step, enough to move a window reflection across the mosaic.
echoes.daria_c1_b: Earlier in your journey: Leena matches the images to the gallery's lighting log.

chapters.title: A Wall in Two Memories
chapters.intro: An inscription appears in an old photograph: a list of adult workers who helped build the gallery. Daria wants to enlarge it for the documentary. Leena points out that one section was painted over while the hall was still open, and that nobody has asked the workers' families what an enlargement would mean. Their disagreement is not about whether the names existed. It is about what the new image will claim.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to make a comparison with explicit gaps or seek accounts before making the enlargement.

choices.label: Make a comparison with explicit gaps
choices.outcome: Daria places the photographs side by side and marks what cannot yet be read. The resulting sequence is less elegant than a restored inscription, but it keeps conjecture separate from evidence. Leena agrees to describe the material changes on camera.
choices.memoryHint: Daria places the photographs side by side and marks what cannot yet be read.

choices.label: Seek accounts before making the enlargement
choices.outcome: Daria contacts adult contributors through the gallery and asks what they want to share. Several recognize a name; one declines further involvement. The enlargement becomes part of a conversation rather than the opening image she had already imagined.
choices.memoryHint: Daria contacts adult contributors through the gallery and asks what they want to share.

echoes.daria_c2_a: Earlier in your journey: The sequence shows repairs accumulated across several decades.
echoes.daria_c2_b: Earlier in your journey: The qualified survey team documents deposits along the raised panel and provides a cautious account of visibility limits.

chapters.title: The Gallery That Stayed
chapters.setting: An empty frame on the quay
chapters.intro: The mosaic did not vanish overnight. Repair, changing water and a later conversion placed it behind the present observation windows. Daria can now explain the square without claiming that every life behind it has been recovered. A small exhibition offers space for either a carefully framed image sequence or an audio-and-image account with contributors. She and Leena agree that the sea is a setting, not an explanation.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to build the image sequence or build an account with contributor voices.

choices.label: Build the image sequence
choices.outcome: Daria exhibits the tests, contact sheets and final photograph together. Visitors can see how position and light alter an apparently certain image. She leaves the unreadable section visible as unreadable, and Leena's name appears beside the restoration notes.
choices.memoryHint: Daria exhibits the tests, contact sheets and final photograph together.

choices.label: Build an account with contributor voices
choices.outcome: Approved recordings accompany the photographs, with transcripts and a quiet image-only route. Some contributors disagree about the hall. Daria keeps the disagreement audible rather than using a voiceover to make it resolve.
choices.memoryHint: Approved recordings accompany the photographs, with transcripts and a quiet image-only route.

echoes.daria_c3_a: Earlier in your journey: Daria places the photographs side by side and marks what cannot yet be read.
echoes.daria_c3_b: Earlier in your journey: Daria contacts adult contributors through the gallery and asks what they want to share.

chapters.title: The Picture Outside the Picture
chapters.intro: A visitor sends Daria a photograph taken on the quay on the day of her celebrated empty-harbor image. Workers fill the edge she cropped away. The sender is not accusing her of removing a person from the original; he asks why the exhibition still calls the harbor abandoned. Daria can begin with a public correction or a new contributor-led sequence. Either way, the old print must stop doing work it cannot support.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to correct the exhibition caption or commission a contributor-led sequence.

choices.label: Correct the exhibition caption
choices.outcome: Daria replaces abandoned with a description of the actual time and view, and explains the misleading crop. She does not pretend the change is invisible. Leena notices that her sister has finally treated a caption as consequential work.
choices.memoryHint: Daria replaces abandoned with a description of the actual time and view, and explains the misleading crop.

choices.label: Commission a contributor-led sequence
choices.outcome: The gallery pays adults connected to the quay to choose additional images and write their own accounts. Daria supplies her contact sheets without requiring the new sequence to end with her photograph.
choices.memoryHint: The gallery pays adults connected to the quay to choose additional images and write their own accounts.

echoes.daria_c4_a: Earlier in your journey: Daria exhibits the tests, contact sheets and final photograph together.
echoes.daria_c4_b: Earlier in your journey: Approved recordings accompany the photographs, with transcripts and a quiet image-only route.

chapters.title: The Camera Left Down
chapters.intro: An adult crew member agrees to discuss the old gallery but declines filming during preparations. Daria has a workable interview and an attractive opening shot she cannot use. Leena suggests recording the empty workbench later, with a clear description of when it was made. Daria can adopt that approach or begin the documentary without a preparation sequence at all. The camera remains in its case while they decide.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to film a clearly identified reconstruction or omit the preparation sequence.

choices.label: Film a clearly identified reconstruction
choices.outcome: Daria records the bench after the work is finished and labels the scene as a later reconstruction. The crew member reviews how his account is used. The film gains an opening image without pretending that permission was broader than it was.
choices.memoryHint: Daria records the bench after the work is finished and labels the scene as a later reconstruction.

choices.label: Omit the preparation sequence
choices.outcome: The film begins with water against the observation glass and the crew member's approved words. A distributor calls the opening quiet. Daria discovers that quiet is a cost she can accept without asking someone else to pay it.
choices.memoryHint: The film begins with water against the observation glass and the crew member's approved words.

echoes.daria_c5_a: Earlier in your journey: Daria replaces abandoned with a description of the actual time and view, and explains the misleading crop.
echoes.daria_c5_b: Earlier in your journey: The gallery pays adults connected to the quay to choose additional images and write their own accounts.

chapters.title: What Leena Remembers
chapters.intro: Leena says the latest cut makes her sound as if she always trusted the project. Daria can quote a release form, but it would answer the wrong question. Their earlier disagreement has become a smooth transition in the edit. Daria can restore it with Leena's participation or remove the personal framing and keep the technical contribution. Neither route entitles her to turn a family argument into a compelling scene.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to restore the disagreement together or keep Leena's contribution technical.

choices.label: Restore the disagreement together
choices.outcome: The sisters revise the sequence and retain a short approved exchange in which their memories remain different. Leena chooses her own final sentence. Daria gives up the easy reconciliation she had written before they actually reached one.
choices.memoryHint: The sisters revise the sequence and retain a short approved exchange in which their memories remain different.

choices.label: Keep Leena's contribution technical
choices.outcome: Daria removes the implied family reconciliation and credits Leena's material expertise plainly. The film loses a neat personal arc, but the sisters can continue their conversation without an audience waiting for its conclusion.
choices.memoryHint: Daria removes the implied family reconciliation and credits Leena's material expertise plainly.

echoes.daria_c6_a: Earlier in your journey: Daria records the bench after the work is finished and labels the scene as a later reconstruction.
echoes.daria_c6_b: Earlier in your journey: The film begins with water against the observation glass and the crew member's approved words.

chapters.title: A Window, Not a Verdict
chapters.intro: The final film can travel as a fixed documentary, carrying a clear record of its limits, or as a changing gallery work with new contributor accounts added over time. The first preserves a coherent account of this investigation. The second accepts uneven updates and more difficult maintenance. Daria looks once more at the mosaic's unreadable square. A window can remain useful without becoming a verdict.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to release the documentary with its limits or keep the gallery work open to revision.

choices.label: Release the documentary with its limits
choices.outcome: The film goes out with source notes, transcripts and a visible correction route. Its unanswered square remains unanswered. Daria watches a screening without explaining the ending afterward; the audience is allowed to notice something she did not frame.
choices.memoryHint: The film goes out with source notes, transcripts and a visible correction route.

choices.label: Keep the gallery work open to revision
choices.outcome: The gallery funds a limited update programme and gives contributors a defined way to add or withdraw material. Daria returns for the next installation as one participant among several. The wall changes, and she no longer calls change a flaw.
choices.memoryHint: The gallery funds a limited update programme and gives contributors a defined way to add or withdraw material.

echoes.daria_c7_a: Earlier in your journey: The sisters revise the sequence and retain a short approved exchange in which their memories remain different.
echoes.daria_c7_b: Earlier in your journey: Daria removes the implied family reconciliation and credits Leena's material expertise plainly.

title: The Cipher That Answers
tagline: The box answers a question you have not asked aloud.
premise: I turned the box once. It returned the question on a card I had not put inside. Shall we look at the hinge before believing the impossible?

chapters.title: A Question in the Hinge
chapters.intro: A small brass-inlaid box returns a card after Lucian turns its ring. The card contains a question he remembers asking his late mentor, though he cannot remember writing it. Neri checks that the box can be examined without forcing it. A seam under the hinge and the paper's cut edge offer separate starting points. Lucian keeps his surprise, but puts aside the word impossible.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to examine the hinge mechanism or examine the card stock.

choices.label: Examine the hinge mechanism
choices.outcome: A shallow compartment holds a second card behind the first. Lucian documents the arrangement without opening the sealed inner section. The mechanism explains how a card could appear; it does not explain why this particular question was waiting.
choices.memoryHint: A shallow compartment holds a second card behind the first.

choices.label: Examine the card stock
choices.outcome: The paper matches a batch used for the mentor's workshop exercises. Lucian finds a faint alignment mark at one corner. Neri proposes a way to compare it without destroying the card, and he lets her finish the explanation.
choices.memoryHint: The paper matches a batch used for the mentor's workshop exercises.

chapters.title: The Shelves That Answer
chapters.setting: A row of linked reading lamps
chapters.intro: The card's alignment marks match a shelf diagram. Turning a harmless demonstration wheel changes which lamps illuminate the collection. Lucian sees a route; Neri sees a reading aid whose labels have become detached. They can reconstruct the old instructions from diagrams or ask adult former workshop participants about using the table. Neither path requires a visitor to perform a test before entering.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to reconstruct the diagrams or invite former participants to explain it.

choices.label: Reconstruct the diagrams
choices.outcome: The drawings separate an optional puzzle route from the ordinary shelf index. Lucian restores both. A mechanism he admired as a secret entrance turns out to have been designed with an uncomplicated alternative all along.
choices.memoryHint: The drawings separate an optional puzzle route from the ordinary shelf index.

choices.label: Invite former participants to explain it
choices.outcome: Adult participants describe different ways they used the lamps, including a direct reading mode. Lucian records accounts with permission and realizes how much of the collection's history was absent from its cleverest-looking objects.
choices.memoryHint: Adult participants describe different ways they used the lamps, including a direct reading mode.

echoes.lucian_c1_a: Earlier in your journey: A shallow compartment holds a second card behind the first.
echoes.lucian_c1_b: Earlier in your journey: The paper matches a batch used for the mentor's workshop exercises.

chapters.title: Neri's Missing Line
chapters.intro: A design sheet bears Lucian's neat title and Neri's rougher engineering notes. It is the puzzle he once presented alone. Neri will discuss the new box, but first asks how the sheet will be described in the catalogue. Lucian can reconstruct their contributions together or add an immediate provisional correction while the details are checked. His embarrassment is not a reason to make her do unpaid explanatory work.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to reconstruct the shared work with Neri or correct the sole-credit claim now.

choices.label: Reconstruct the shared work with Neri
choices.outcome: The library pays for a documented review. Their accounts do not agree on every detail, but the catalogue identifies both contributions and preserves that uncertainty. Neri returns to the box as a contracted colleague rather than a helpful footnote.
choices.memoryHint: The library pays for a documented review.

choices.label: Correct the sole-credit claim now
choices.outcome: Lucian removes the claim that the design was his alone and publishes a provisional account pending paid review. The correction is less complete than he wants. Neri appreciates that incompleteness has not become another reason to delay it.
choices.memoryHint: Lucian removes the claim that the design was his alone and publishes a provisional account pending paid review.

echoes.lucian_c2_a: Earlier in your journey: The drawings separate an optional puzzle route from the ordinary shelf index.
echoes.lucian_c2_b: Earlier in your journey: Adult participants describe different ways they used the lamps, including a direct reading mode.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Unfinished Set
chapters.intro: With permission from the collection's custodian, the inner section is opened. It holds workshop questions arranged to be selected by the ring's position. Lucian recognizes the question because he helped sort the cards years ago. The box did not read his mind. The mentor left a mechanism for returning to familiar questions, and enough unfinished cards for someone else to continue. The library must decide how visitors encounter it.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to offer an optional guided puzzle or display the mechanism openly.

choices.label: Offer an optional guided puzzle
choices.outcome: The library explains what the box does without spoiling every route. Visitors can solve it, ask for assistance or read the mechanism directly. Lucian begins the first session by making those options ordinary rather than announcing them as exceptions.
choices.memoryHint: The library explains what the box does without spoiling every route.

choices.label: Display the mechanism openly
choices.outcome: The compartment is shown beside the cards, with a separate hands-on replica for visitors. The surprise changes from a hidden answer to the care of the construction. Neri points out that knowing how it works has not made it less interesting.
choices.memoryHint: The compartment is shown beside the cards, with a separate hands-on replica for visitors.

echoes.lucian_c3_a: Earlier in your journey: The library pays for a documented review.
echoes.lucian_c3_b: Earlier in your journey: Lucian removes the claim that the design was his alone and publishes a provisional account pending paid review.

chapters.title: The Card Without a Match
chapters.intro: A new card arrives with a question absent from the workshop set. Its sender offers no name, only a drawing that fits the demonstration table. Lucian is tempted to announce the mentor's final puzzle. Neri asks how a living contributor might feel about being credited to someone else. They can invite the sender to clarify the proposal or examine the drawing as an unattributed submission first.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to invite a bounded conversation or review the drawing without attribution claims.

choices.label: Invite a bounded conversation
choices.outcome: The library posts a neutral request for the sender to contact it, without publishing identifying clues. An adult maker answers and asks to remain unnamed. Lucian offers the same submission terms used for named contributors.
choices.memoryHint: The library posts a neutral request for the sender to contact it, without publishing identifying clues.

choices.label: Review the drawing without attribution claims
choices.outcome: Lucian labels the design as an unsolicited modern submission and tests a paper model. He does not attach the mentor's name to its appeal. The sender later contacts Neri, encouraged that the library has left room for a living author.
choices.memoryHint: Lucian labels the design as an unsolicited modern submission and tests a paper model.

echoes.lucian_c4_a: Earlier in your journey: The library explains what the box does without spoiling every route.
echoes.lucian_c4_b: Earlier in your journey: The compartment is shown beside the cards, with a separate hands-on replica for visitors.

chapters.title: A Puzzle That Can Refuse
chapters.intro: The submitted design includes a route that ends without opening the last compartment. Lucian initially calls it the wrong solution. Neri asks him to demonstrate where the instructions promised that every route must reveal everything. They can revise the visitor guide to acknowledge a legitimate stopping point or make a separate model that clearly teaches the mechanism without using the private compartment at all.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to make stopping a stated route or build a transparent teaching model.

choices.label: Make stopping a stated route
choices.outcome: The guide identifies the stopping point without ranking it below the opening route. Visitors leave with different experiences of the same box. Lucian hears someone say they enjoyed not being required to finish, and resists turning that response into a new test.
choices.memoryHint: The guide identifies the stopping point without ranking it below the opening route.

choices.label: Build a transparent teaching model
choices.outcome: A new model shows the mechanism while the submitted private compartment remains closed. The library pays the maker for the separate design. Explanation becomes possible without claiming that access to one object entails access to every part of it.
choices.memoryHint: A new model shows the mechanism while the submitted private compartment remains closed.

echoes.lucian_c5_a: Earlier in your journey: The library posts a neutral request for the sender to contact it, without publishing identifying clues.
echoes.lucian_c5_b: Earlier in your journey: Lucian labels the design as an unsolicited modern submission and tests a paper model.

chapters.title: The Answer He Wanted
chapters.intro: A recording from Lucian's sole-credit lecture resurfaces in the library's introductory material. Its correction exists in the catalogue but not in the video. Neri has already named the mismatch once. Lucian can replace the introduction or preserve the old recording with a clear, inseparable correction and a new introduction by the design team. Keeping it unchanged is no longer a neutral default.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to replace the old introduction or keep the record with an inseparable correction.

choices.label: Replace the old introduction
choices.outcome: The library removes the promotional cut and commissions a new explanation with agreed credit. The original remains in restricted institutional records. Lucian gives up the version in which he sounds most certain and discovers that he can teach without it.
choices.memoryHint: The library removes the promotional cut and commissions a new explanation with agreed credit.

choices.label: Keep the record with an inseparable correction
choices.outcome: The old lecture is retained only with a prominent correction and an agreed new introduction. Neri can decline appearing in it. Viewers encounter both the error and the repair, without being asked to treat the repair as a triumph.
choices.memoryHint: The old lecture is retained only with a prominent correction and an agreed new introduction.

echoes.lucian_c6_a: Earlier in your journey: The guide identifies the stopping point without ranking it below the opening route.
echoes.lucian_c6_b: Earlier in your journey: A new model shows the mechanism while the submitted private compartment remains closed.

chapters.title: Questions Worth Keeping
chapters.setting: The table before the next workshop
chapters.intro: The library can become a working studio for new puzzles or keep its collection-focused programme with occasional paid commissions. Lucian likes the liveliness of the first and the continuity of the second. Neri asks him to choose the workload he can actually support rather than the most impressive future. On the table lies the original card. Its question has not changed; his answer has.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to build a paid puzzle studio or keep a careful collection programme.

choices.label: Build a paid puzzle studio
choices.outcome: A smaller exhibition makes space for paid making sessions, clear credit and accessible routes through new designs. Lucian works alongside contributors whose solutions are better than his first ideas. The box becomes the beginning of a practice rather than its untouchable masterpiece.
choices.memoryHint: A smaller exhibition makes space for paid making sessions, clear credit and accessible routes through new designs.

choices.label: Keep a careful collection programme
choices.outcome: The library funds a sustainable schedule of conservation, demonstrations and occasional paid new work. It turns down projects it cannot support properly. Lucian keeps a blank card in the case, labeled as space for a future question rather than a promise already made.
choices.memoryHint: The library funds a sustainable schedule of conservation, demonstrations and occasional paid new work.

echoes.lucian_c7_a: Earlier in your journey: The library removes the promotional cut and commissions a new explanation with agreed credit.
echoes.lucian_c7_b: Earlier in your journey: The old lecture is retained only with a prominent correction and an agreed new introduction.

title: The Mountain’s Second Shadow
tagline: At sunset, one mountain casts two shadows.
premise: One ridge, two shadows. The second arrives after the first has stopped moving. I would like to write that down before deciding what it means.

chapters.title: Two Shadows at Dusk
chapters.intro: From the shelter window, a second ridge-shaped shadow crosses the crater lake after the mountain's own shadow has settled. Ansel records its arrival on a wall chart. Maeve has permission to compare observations from the shelter; she does not have a reason to leave the approved paths. A timed drawing and the old optical equipment offer two useful places to begin.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to compare the timed drawings or inspect the stored optical equipment.

choices.label: Compare the timed drawings
choices.outcome: The second outline follows the position of a partly obscured reflector on the old observatory ridge. Maeve marks a possible connection rather than a conclusion. Ansel adds the days on which the outline failed to appear.
choices.memoryHint: The second outline follows the position of a partly obscured reflector on the old observatory ridge.

choices.label: Inspect the stored optical equipment
choices.outcome: A boxed lens carries an alignment pattern resembling the extra outline. Maeve checks the inventory before calling it missing equipment. The records suggest an abandoned light experiment that used the lake as part of its demonstration.
choices.memoryHint: A boxed lens carries an alignment pattern resembling the extra outline.

chapters.title: The Shelter's Other Window
chapters.intro: A sealed side window appears on the original shelter plan but not on the visitor diagram. Through the authorized interior inspection, Maeve finds a removable panel and old projection fittings. Ansel remembers a weather demonstration, though not its purpose. They can search the instrument records or compare the panel's view with existing photographs. The mountain remains outside the room, less interested in their explanation than they are.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to read the instrument records or compare photographs from the window.

choices.label: Read the instrument records
choices.outcome: A maintenance book describes repeated alignment problems in the demonstration system. Maeve finds several proposed explanations, each crossed out by its author. The old team was less certain than the visitor account had made them sound.
choices.memoryHint: A maintenance book describes repeated alignment problems in the demonstration system.

choices.label: Compare photographs from the window
choices.outcome: The images show the lake at different levels, shifting the apparent outline across the surface. Maeve can reproduce part of the effect in a safe tabletop model, without treating that model as a complete account of the island.
choices.memoryHint: The images show the lake at different levels, shifting the apparent outline across the surface.

echoes.maeve_c1_a: Earlier in your journey: The second outline follows the position of a partly obscured reflector on the old observatory ridge.
echoes.maeve_c1_b: Earlier in your journey: A boxed lens carries an alignment pattern resembling the extra outline.

chapters.title: Ansel's Unfinished Repair
chapters.intro: Ansel produces a replacement bracket he made years after the demonstration closed. Maeve had assumed the optical system was untouched since its last official service. It was not. Ansel wants the repair described accurately, including the permission under which he made it. Maeve can add his account to the equipment history or begin a joint inventory that distinguishes original parts from later maintenance.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to record the repair account or make the inventory together.

choices.label: Record the repair account
choices.outcome: Ansel approves a plain account of the repair and its limits. It explains one change in the projection without making him the author of the whole effect. Maeve revises a sentence that had implied the system was abandoned completely.
choices.memoryHint: Ansel approves a plain account of the repair and its limits.

choices.label: Make the inventory together
choices.outcome: The paid inventory identifies original components, Ansel's repair and several unrecorded replacements. Maeve sees a maintained place rather than a frozen historical scene. Ansel points out a worn hinge that matters more to his daily work than the famous lens.
choices.memoryHint: The paid inventory identifies original components, Ansel's repair and several unrecorded replacements.

echoes.maeve_c2_a: Earlier in your journey: A maintenance book describes repeated alignment problems in the demonstration system.
echoes.maeve_c2_b: Earlier in your journey: The images show the lake at different levels, shifting the apparent outline across the surface.

chapters.title: The Shadow Explained, In Part
chapters.intro: Their model explains how the old projection could make a ridge-like outline move across the lake. It does not reproduce every night's observation. The visitor centre wants a confident account for the season's opening. Maeve can present the partial explanation with an observation programme or build a demonstration clearly separated from the unresolved field observations. Neither option restores the certainty of the old sign.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to present a partial explanation openly or separate demonstration from investigation.

choices.label: Present a partial explanation openly
choices.outcome: The centre displays the known mechanism, the mismatches and a funded observation schedule. Visitors can contribute only from approved viewing areas. Maeve begins her talk with the part her model does not explain, and finds that attention survives the admission.
choices.memoryHint: The centre displays the known mechanism, the mismatches and a funded observation schedule.

choices.label: Separate demonstration from investigation
choices.outcome: A tabletop exhibit teaches the optical effect while a distinct panel describes the ongoing island study. The labels stop using the word solved. Ansel keeps his wall chart in use rather than donating it as the relic of a finished mystery.
choices.memoryHint: A tabletop exhibit teaches the optical effect while a distinct panel describes the ongoing island study.

echoes.maeve_c3_a: Earlier in your journey: Ansel approves a plain account of the repair and its limits.
echoes.maeve_c3_b: Earlier in your journey: The paid inventory identifies original components, Ansel's repair and several unrecorded replacements.

chapters.title: A Day Without the Outline
chapters.intro: The expected outline does not appear. The instruments report no fault that explains its absence, and a new photograph shows a pale seam on the far ridge. Maeve can compare existing observations with the qualified survey team's account or ask for a separately authorized inspection when conditions permit. She does not turn a strange photograph into a public hazard announcement on her own authority.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to compare the observation records first or request an authorized inspection.

choices.label: Compare the observation records first
choices.outcome: The comparison identifies several similar absences in older charts. Maeve shares the pattern with the authorized team, including its limits. A dramatic evening becomes part of a longer record rather than an isolated omen.
choices.memoryHint: The comparison identifies several similar absences in older charts.

choices.label: Request an authorized inspection
choices.outcome: The local team decides the timing and scope of the inspection. Their report documents a changed surface near the old reflector, without endorsing every hypothesis about it. Maeve incorporates the findings and credits the decisions she did not make.
choices.memoryHint: The local team decides the timing and scope of the inspection.

echoes.maeve_c4_a: Earlier in your journey: The centre displays the known mechanism, the mismatches and a funded observation schedule.
echoes.maeve_c4_b: Earlier in your journey: A tabletop exhibit teaches the optical effect while a distinct panel describes the ongoing island study.

chapters.title: The Map With a Confident Edge
chapters.intro: A visitor brings Maeve's early survey, the one whose confident summary travelled farther than its correction. It marks the old demonstration area as fully documented. Ansel has been using that map to explain why he kept his own notes. Maeve can issue a new edition with a conspicuous correction or make the older map part of an exhibit about how the account changed.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to issue a corrected edition or exhibit the changing account.

choices.label: Issue a corrected edition
choices.outcome: The new map distinguishes observed areas, uncertain boundaries and later repairs. Maeve names the overstatement in the original summary without hiding it in an appendix. Ansel receives copies for the shelter before the public launch.
choices.memoryHint: The new map distinguishes observed areas, uncertain boundaries and later repairs.

choices.label: Exhibit the changing account
choices.outcome: The centre shows the old map beside its correction and the caretaker's records. Maeve pays for reproducing the local material rather than treating it as a free supporting illustration. Visitors can see why a complete-looking border did not make the work complete.
choices.memoryHint: The centre shows the old map beside its correction and the caretaker's records.

echoes.maeve_c5_a: Earlier in your journey: The comparison identifies several similar absences in older charts.
echoes.maeve_c5_b: Earlier in your journey: The local team decides the timing and scope of the inspection.

chapters.title: Who Gets the View
chapters.intro: The new research has drawn more visitors to a shelter with limited staff and fragile paths. Ansel likes sharing the place and dislikes becoming its permanent unpaid guide. The island team is considering a smaller staffed viewing programme or a research-focused season with remote exhibits. Maeve must recommend what her project can support, not what would make the best closing photograph.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to support a smaller staffed programme or support a research-focused season.

choices.label: Support a smaller staffed programme
choices.outcome: The project funds limited guided sessions under local access rules. Fewer people visit at once, and some cannot get the date they want. Maeve explains the limits in the publicity instead of leaving the caretakers to disappoint arrivals at the door.
choices.memoryHint: The project funds limited guided sessions under local access rules.

choices.label: Support a research-focused season
choices.outcome: The centre expands its remote exhibit and reduces on-site promotion while the team works. The quieter season costs some local income, which the project addresses through paid documentation work rather than a promise that attention will eventually compensate everyone.
choices.memoryHint: The centre expands its remote exhibit and reduces on-site promotion while the team works.

echoes.maeve_c6_a: Earlier in your journey: The new map distinguishes observed areas, uncertain boundaries and later repairs.
echoes.maeve_c6_b: Earlier in your journey: The centre shows the old map beside its correction and the caretaker's records.

chapters.title: The Mountain Remains
chapters.setting: The shelter at the season's end
chapters.intro: Maeve has a better account of the second shadow and an honest list of what remains uncertain. The project can continue as a small recurring study or conclude this funded phase with a usable handover. She is tempted to promise both. Ansel asks which work she will still be able to answer for after leaving the island. The light on the lake shifts while she considers a smaller, more durable ending.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to fund a recurring observation partnership or finish with a complete handover.

choices.label: Fund a recurring observation partnership
choices.outcome: The next phase has named responsibilities, paid local work and a schedule Maeve can keep. The outline becomes one observation among many, not a spectacle that has to happen on demand. She leaves a spare notebook rather than another definitive sign.
choices.memoryHint: The next phase has named responsibilities, paid local work and a schedule Maeve can keep.

choices.label: Finish with a complete handover
choices.outcome: Maeve closes the funded phase with maintained records, clear uncertainties and agreed ownership of equipment and data. Ansel can continue his chart without being enrolled in an indefinite research promise. The mountain keeps its second shadow without owing her another chapter.
choices.memoryHint: Maeve closes the funded phase with maintained records, clear uncertainties and agreed ownership of equipment and data.

echoes.maeve_c7_a: Earlier in your journey: The project funds limited guided sessions under local access rules.
echoes.maeve_c7_b: Earlier in your journey: The centre expands its remote exhibit and reduces on-site promotion while the team works.

title: The Room With Two Exits
tagline: Two doors lead to the same room, but not the same story.
premise: I have walked through both doors. I arrived at the same chair, facing opposite windows. Before we call it impossible, let us look at the floor plan.

chapters.title: The Second Exit
chapters.intro: The theatre's old room illusion has two doors where the surviving drawing shows one. Idris enters only after the inspection team clears the room for a supervised visit. Each doorway seems to return him to the same chair with a different window behind it. Noor asks him to describe what he observed before naming the trick. They can compare the drawings or trace the harmless demonstration model left on a shelf.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to compare the surviving drawings or examine the demonstration model.

choices.label: Compare the surviving drawings
choices.outcome: A later plan adds a rotated stage unit, but its annotations are in another hand. Idris records the addition without assigning it to the famous designer on the title page. The extra door begins to look like a revision rather than a miracle.
choices.memoryHint: A later plan adds a rotated stage unit, but its annotations are in another hand.

choices.label: Examine the demonstration model
choices.outcome: The paper model turns a wall into a window when its base rotates. Noor points out a missing stop in the model, not a defect to reproduce on stage. The model explains a principle while leaving the real room's construction for qualified inspection.
choices.memoryHint: The paper model turns a wall into a window when its base rotates.

chapters.title: The Window in the Wrong Wall
chapters.intro: A painted window frame appears in three production photographs, each supposedly from a different side of the room. The frame survives in storage with two sets of mounting marks. Idris wants to reconstruct the effect; Noor wants the production records located before anything is moved. They can follow the frame's inventory or ask an adult former scene painter about the photographs.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to follow the inventory trail or ask the scene painter.

choices.label: Follow the inventory trail
choices.outcome: The frame moved between productions and was repainted rather than rebuilt. Idris finds a repair entry naming a workshop team omitted from the souvenir programme. A single celebrated illusion turns out to have a longer working life.
choices.memoryHint: The frame moved between productions and was repainted rather than rebuilt.

choices.label: Ask the scene painter
choices.outcome: The former painter explains the changing view with a tabletop sketch and agrees to a recorded account of her own work. She declines to explain another maker's mechanism. Idris keeps those two permissions separate in his notes.
choices.memoryHint: The former painter explains the changing view with a tabletop sketch and agrees to a recorded account of her own work.

echoes.idris_c1_a: Earlier in your journey: A later plan adds a rotated stage unit, but its annotations are in another hand.
echoes.idris_c1_b: Earlier in your journey: The paper model turns a wall into a window when its base rotates.

chapters.title: Noor's Margin
chapters.setting: A programme with an empty credit
chapters.intro: Noor brings Idris the programme from their early success. It names him as designer and describes her engineering as assistance. He remembers approving that wording because the deadline was close. The revived room offers a chance to repeat the arrangement under a better-looking caption or change how decisions are actually made. Before choosing a final credit, Idris asks what work Noor wants to take on now.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to negotiate a new shared design role or commission Noor for a defined scope.

choices.label: Negotiate a new shared design role
choices.outcome: Noor agrees to a paid role with authority over the revival's engineering and an explicit place in design decisions. They keep the old credit error in the project record. A more accurate new programme will follow an actual working change.
choices.memoryHint: Noor agrees to a paid role with authority over the revival's engineering and an explicit place in design decisions.

choices.label: Commission Noor for a defined scope
choices.outcome: Noor chooses a narrower paid scope and keeps the right to decline additional work. Idris stops treating limited involvement as a rejection of the whole project. The new credit states her contribution without implying endorsement of every performance decision.
choices.memoryHint: Noor chooses a narrower paid scope and keeps the right to decline additional work.

echoes.idris_c2_a: Earlier in your journey: The frame moved between productions and was repainted rather than rebuilt.
echoes.idris_c2_b: Earlier in your journey: The former painter explains the changing view with a tabletop sketch and agrees to a recorded account of her own work.

chapters.title: The Room Learns Its Shape
chapters.intro: The inspection and records support a practical explanation of the double-door effect. There will be no public revival until the theatre's own technical team approves its construction and operation. Idris can now develop a performance that preserves surprise or an explanatory installation that shows the model openly. Noor asks him which audience experience he wants to be responsible for, rather than which will make him seem cleverer.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to develop a consent-based performance or develop an explanatory installation.

choices.label: Develop a consent-based performance
choices.outcome: The invitation clearly presents a staged illusion, offers a plain alternative route and leaves the mechanism a performance secret. Idris begins rehearsing the audience's experience rather than a claim that the room breaks reality.
choices.memoryHint: The invitation clearly presents a staged illusion, offers a plain alternative route and leaves the mechanism a performance secret.

choices.label: Develop an explanatory installation
choices.outcome: A working model and approved design records show how changing viewpoints create the effect. Noor decides what may be disclosed from her work. The installation trades a moment of surprise for a longer pleasure of understanding.
choices.memoryHint: A working model and approved design records show how changing viewpoints create the effect.

echoes.idris_c3_a: Earlier in your journey: Noor agrees to a paid role with authority over the revival's engineering and an explicit place in design decisions.
echoes.idris_c3_b: Earlier in your journey: Noor chooses a narrower paid scope and keeps the right to decline additional work.

chapters.title: The Patron's Extra Condition
chapters.setting: A contract on the rehearsal table
chapters.intro: A patron offers enough support to complete the project, provided the publicity calls the room an unsolved phenomenon. Idris could propose accurate performance wording or seek a smaller production through other support. The patron may accept the change, or not. Noor reads the sentence aloud without theatrical emphasis, making its ordinary dishonesty harder to disguise.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to negotiate accurate publicity or choose a smaller independent production.

choices.label: Negotiate accurate publicity
choices.outcome: Idris proposes an extraordinary staged experience instead of an unexplained real phenomenon. The patron accepts less sensational wording in exchange for a smaller opening event. Noor agrees that the compromise preserves the essential distinction.
choices.memoryHint: Idris proposes an extraordinary staged experience instead of an unexplained real phenomenon.

choices.label: Choose a smaller independent production
choices.outcome: The team reduces the scope and seeks support under truthful publicity. Some planned features are postponed. Idris gives up the opening he had pictured, but does not ask the audience to fund it with a misunderstanding.
choices.memoryHint: The team reduces the scope and seeks support under truthful publicity.

echoes.idris_c4_a: Earlier in your journey: The invitation clearly presents a staged illusion, offers a plain alternative route and leaves the mechanism a performance secret.
echoes.idris_c4_b: Earlier in your journey: A working model and approved design records show how changing viewpoints create the effect.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal That Stops
chapters.intro: During an approved rehearsal, a demonstration element does not behave as expected. The theatre's technical lead pauses the session. Idris has no authority to wave the interruption away, though he can decide what the waiting preview group is told. He can give a straightforward explanation and reschedule, or offer a different approved demonstration that does not use the affected element.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to explain and reschedule or offer the separate approved model.

choices.label: Explain and reschedule
choices.outcome: Idris tells the group that the intended demonstration is paused and offers the theatre's rescheduling options. He does not call the fault part of the mystery. Noor later says the plain explanation did more for the project than a perfect improvisation would have.
choices.memoryHint: Idris tells the group that the intended demonstration is paused and offers the theatre's rescheduling options.

choices.label: Offer the separate approved model
choices.outcome: With the technical lead's agreement, the team shows the independent tabletop model instead. Idris explains why it is a different experience rather than pretending nobody will notice. The group leaves with questions the original performance would have hidden.
choices.memoryHint: With the technical lead's agreement, the team shows the independent tabletop model instead.

echoes.idris_c5_a: Earlier in your journey: Idris proposes an extraordinary staged experience instead of an unexplained real phenomenon.
echoes.idris_c5_b: Earlier in your journey: The team reduces the scope and seeks support under truthful publicity.

chapters.title: The Unused Invitation
chapters.intro: Noor declines an invitation to speak at the opening. She wants the agreed credit and payment, not a public scene of reconciliation. Idris had imagined thanking her under the lights. He can ask how she wants the contribution acknowledged or keep the agreed programme credit and direct his opening remarks toward the whole working team. Her absence is not an invitation to explain her motives.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to ask for her preferred acknowledgment or keep the agreed credit without a personal tribute.

choices.label: Ask for her preferred acknowledgment
choices.outcome: Noor approves a short factual acknowledgment and declines the personal anecdote Idris suggests. He follows her wording without adding a flourish. Their trust improves in a conversation the audience never hears.
choices.memoryHint: Noor approves a short factual acknowledgment and declines the personal anecdote Idris suggests.

choices.label: Keep the agreed credit without a personal tribute
choices.outcome: Idris retains the programme credit and acknowledges the team collectively in the agreed form. The empty seat remains ordinary. Later, Noor asks to see a rehearsal recording rather than hear a description of how much he missed her.
choices.memoryHint: Idris retains the programme credit and acknowledges the team collectively in the agreed form.

echoes.idris_c6_a: Earlier in your journey: Idris tells the group that the intended demonstration is paused and offers the theatre's rescheduling options.
echoes.idris_c6_b: Earlier in your journey: With the technical lead's agreement, the team shows the independent tabletop model instead.

chapters.title: A Door Left Ordinary
chapters.intro: The approved work is ready. The theatre can keep the room as a recurring performance or make it a temporary installation whose materials return to the workshop afterward. Idris enjoys the possibility of a signature show, but has learned that a project can end without failing. Either future needs agreed work, clear credit and an audience invited to wonder rather than commanded to believe.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to keep a recurring performance or let the installation have a real ending.

choices.label: Keep a recurring performance
choices.outcome: The theatre schedules a sustainable run under the technical team's conditions and the makers' contracts. Idris shares the introduction with another performer. Two doors still surprise the audience, while an ordinary exit remains unmistakably available.
choices.memoryHint: The theatre schedules a sustainable run under the technical team's conditions and the makers' contracts.

choices.label: Let the installation have a real ending
choices.outcome: The room runs for a defined season, then its agreed components return to their makers. Idris keeps the paper model rather than claiming permanent ownership of the whole illusion. The final audience leaves through one ordinary door, still arguing cheerfully about the other.
choices.memoryHint: The room runs for a defined season, then its agreed components return to their makers.

echoes.idris_c7_a: Earlier in your journey: Noor approves a short factual acknowledgment and declines the personal anecdote Idris suggests.
echoes.idris_c7_b: Earlier in your journey: Idris retains the programme credit and acknowledges the team collectively in the agreed form.

title: The Garden in Orbit
tagline: An abandoned garden still receives one careful visitor.
premise: This unit returns to the empty drawer every cycle. The routine is real. Whether the drawer is empty is the part I would like to check.

chapters.title: The Empty Seed Drawer
chapters.intro: During an authorized salvage survey, a small maintenance robot repeats a watering route that ends at an empty drawer. The station's records describe the drawer as cleared years ago. Rhea and Ren remain in the areas the crew has released for inspection. They can compare the robot's route log or examine the drawer's external inventory marks. Rhea avoids giving the routine a story before finding what it actually does.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to compare the route logs or examine the inventory marks.

choices.label: Compare the route logs
choices.outcome: The last instruction update predates the drawer's clearance record. Rhea identifies a mismatch rather than an act of machine loyalty. One scheduled stop includes a different drawer code, pointing toward an inventory change no one completed.
choices.memoryHint: The last instruction update predates the drawer's clearance record.

choices.label: Examine the inventory marks
choices.outcome: A replaced label covers an older identifier. Ren documents it without disturbing the sealed inner compartment. Rhea finds that empty may describe the current database entry, not everything physically associated with the drawer.
choices.memoryHint: A replaced label covers an older identifier.

chapters.title: A Garden on Borrowed Light
chapters.intro: The released records show that the greenhouse ran on a reduced maintenance plan before decommissioning. Several systems were described as expendable in a summary Rhea has been using as her salvage guide. Ren finds a longer schedule naming a preserved seed study. They can reconstruct the inventory history or ask the authorized station team to review the study's remaining storage. Neither route requires improvising work on unreleased equipment.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to reconstruct the inventory history or request a storage review.

choices.label: Reconstruct the inventory history
choices.outcome: Rhea traces the drawer's identifier through several database migrations. The study was not deliberately erased, but its connection to the physical compartment was lost. Ren marks each inference so the new inventory will not inherit another confident shortcut.
choices.memoryHint: Rhea traces the drawer's identifier through several database migrations.

choices.label: Request a storage review
choices.outcome: The authorized team confirms a small sealed study compartment and defines what can be examined. Its contents are not automatically viable or valuable. Rhea begins a preservation plan with those uncertainties intact.
choices.memoryHint: The authorized team confirms a small sealed study compartment and defines what can be examined.

echoes.rhea_c1_a: Earlier in your journey: The last instruction update predates the drawer's clearance record.
echoes.rhea_c1_b: Earlier in your journey: A replaced label covers an older identifier.

chapters.title: Ren's Two Other Options
chapters.intro: Rhea's first proposal saves the study compartment by sacrificing two functioning survey units. Ren lays out two alternatives: a slower transfer using contracted equipment, or a narrower preservation task within the current resources. Both have costs. Rhea recognizes the ease with which she has begun calling her own proposal inevitable. She can investigate the slower transfer or make the reduced scope explicit before asking anyone to agree.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to develop the slower transfer plan or define a smaller preservation task.

choices.label: Develop the slower transfer plan
choices.outcome: The team secures qualified support and a longer approved work window. Some salvage goals are postponed. Rhea records the trade-off as a decision, not proof that time and money cease to matter when a plan is careful.
choices.memoryHint: The team secures qualified support and a longer approved work window.

choices.label: Define a smaller preservation task
choices.outcome: The team documents what the present resources can preserve and what they cannot promise. Rhea removes the word rescue from the publicity until outcomes are known. Ren finds that her plan is easier to improve once it admits its boundaries.
choices.memoryHint: The team documents what the present resources can preserve and what they cannot promise.

echoes.rhea_c2_a: Earlier in your journey: Rhea traces the drawer's identifier through several database migrations.
echoes.rhea_c2_b: Earlier in your journey: The authorized team confirms a small sealed study compartment and defines what can be examined.

chapters.title: What the Drawer Contains
chapters.intro: The compartment holds a fictional plant study, old growth records and a small set of preserved material awaiting specialist evaluation. The robot's routine maintained conditions around the compartment, not the miracle Rhea had briefly imagined. The project can prioritize a careful transfer of the preserved material or a fuller documentation package while the station team maintains the compartment for an agreed interval.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to prioritize specialist transfer or prioritize a fuller record first.

choices.label: Prioritize specialist transfer
choices.outcome: The material moves through the authorized specialist process with its incomplete records attached. Rhea keeps a record of the maintenance routine as evidence of what the unit did, without naming it a human promise. The garden's future moves beyond her own workshop.
choices.memoryHint: The material moves through the authorized specialist process with its incomplete records attached.

choices.label: Prioritize a fuller record first
choices.outcome: The team funds an agreed maintenance interval while it assembles the study history for specialist review. The delay is documented rather than described as risk-free. Ren's inventory work becomes as visible as the attractive images of leaves against the planet.
choices.memoryHint: The team funds an agreed maintenance interval while it assembles the study history for specialist review.

echoes.rhea_c3_a: Earlier in your journey: The team secures qualified support and a longer approved work window.
echoes.rhea_c3_b: Earlier in your journey: The team documents what the present resources can preserve and what they cannot promise.

chapters.title: A Root Through the Diagram
chapters.intro: A new survey finds that one plant rail connects two zones the summary diagram treated as separate. The connection is part of the fictional greenhouse's old experimental layout. Rhea can compare the original drawings or ask the specialist team to review the new survey before revising the salvage plan. She has learned not to let a surprising photograph do the work of a complete systems account.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to compare the original layout records or seek a specialist review of the survey.

choices.label: Compare the original layout records
choices.outcome: The drawings show a planned shared rail whose later modifications were never consolidated. Rhea produces a marked comparison, not an executable repair instruction. The station team can now assess the connection with a clearer history.
choices.memoryHint: The drawings show a planned shared rail whose later modifications were never consolidated.

choices.label: Seek a specialist review of the survey
choices.outcome: The review identifies what can be inferred and what still needs authorized examination. Rhea keeps the slower response in the project timeline. A less dramatic update gives the crew something useful to make decisions with.
choices.memoryHint: The review identifies what can be inferred and what still needs authorized examination.

echoes.rhea_c4_a: Earlier in your journey: The material moves through the authorized specialist process with its incomplete records attached.
echoes.rhea_c4_b: Earlier in your journey: The team funds an agreed maintenance interval while it assembles the study history for specialist review.

chapters.title: The Unit She Cannibalized
chapters.setting: A message from an old colleague
chapters.intro: A former colleague sends Rhea photographs of the survey units she stripped during her earlier repair. One has since been restored from spare parts she did not know existed. The message does not say that her exhausted choice was easy or uniquely wrong. It asks her to stop teaching it as the only possible answer. Rhea can revise the workshop account or invite the colleague to help develop a broader repair exercise.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to revise the workshop account or develop the exercise with her colleague.

choices.label: Revise the workshop account
choices.outcome: Rhea adds the missing alternatives and the conditions under which she made the original decision. She does not convert the revision into a story about never making mistakes again. Ren notices the next proposal leaves room for someone else to contribute.
choices.memoryHint: Rhea adds the missing alternatives and the conditions under which she made the original decision.

choices.label: Develop the exercise with her colleague
choices.outcome: The colleague agrees to paid work on an exercise with several defensible approaches and explicit limits. Rhea teaches one session as a participant rather than the person holding the final answer. The old repair becomes a case to examine, not a legend.
choices.memoryHint: The colleague agrees to paid work on an exercise with several defensible approaches and explicit limits.

echoes.rhea_c5_a: Earlier in your journey: The drawings show a planned shared rail whose later modifications were never consolidated.
echoes.rhea_c5_b: Earlier in your journey: The review identifies what can be inferred and what still needs authorized examination.

chapters.title: A Place for the Routine
chapters.intro: The robot can be reassigned after the garden project or retained as part of an approved educational display. Rhea feels an attachment to its repeated route. That feeling belongs to her; it does not decide the unit's capabilities, resources or safe use. She and Ren can recommend useful continued service or a clearly explained display that preserves the route's history without presenting it as a grieving machine.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to recommend continued practical service or recommend a clearly explained display.

choices.label: Recommend continued practical service
choices.outcome: The authorized team evaluates a new task and documents the unit's limits before reassignment. Rhea keeps the route records in the study archive. She is glad to see the machine work again without asking its new job to reproduce her favorite story.
choices.memoryHint: The authorized team evaluates a new task and documents the unit's limits before reassignment.

choices.label: Recommend a clearly explained display
choices.outcome: The display explains the routine, the inventory mismatch and the human work of the preservation project. It makes no claim that the unit experienced abandonment. Rhea helps build a demonstration people can understand without having to attribute a human life to it.
choices.memoryHint: The display explains the routine, the inventory mismatch and the human work of the preservation project.

echoes.rhea_c6_a: Earlier in your journey: Rhea adds the missing alternatives and the conditions under which she made the original decision.
echoes.rhea_c6_b: Earlier in your journey: The colleague agrees to paid work on an exercise with several defensible approaches and explicit limits.

chapters.title: The Garden She Can Carry
chapters.intro: The approved next phase offers two futures: a compact off-station study collection or a smaller, properly supported orbital greenhouse programme. The first carries records and selected material to a place with established support. The second preserves the extraordinary setting at a continuing cost. Rhea wants both, but the handover asks what this team can actually sustain. Ren waits beside a plan that has room for signatures other than hers.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to build the portable study collection or support the smaller orbital programme.

choices.label: Build the portable study collection
choices.outcome: The project transfers the agreed records and material to a supported study collection, keeping the orbital history intact. Rhea packs the final inventory beside the first mistaken diagram. The garden becomes smaller and easier to care for, without pretending nothing was left behind.
choices.memoryHint: The project transfers the agreed records and material to a supported study collection, keeping the orbital history intact.

choices.label: Support the smaller orbital programme
choices.outcome: A funded team takes responsibility for a reduced greenhouse programme with clear work and review intervals. Rhea returns as an engineer when contracted, not as the garden's indispensable savior. Through the curved window, the planet continues turning without waiting for her repair.
choices.memoryHint: A funded team takes responsibility for a reduced greenhouse programme with clear work and review intervals.

echoes.rhea_c7_a: Earlier in your journey: The authorized team evaluates a new task and documents the unit's limits before reassignment.
echoes.rhea_c7_b: Earlier in your journey: The display explains the routine, the inventory mismatch and the human work of the preservation project.

title: The Perfume of Rain
tagline: A bottle recalls rain from a courtyard that no longer exists.
premise: This bottle reminds me of rain in a courtyard I knew. Salome says it reminds her of a warm cupboard. We should probably begin by allowing both descriptions.

chapters.title: Rain in a Closed Bottle
chapters.setting: The scent archive after a storm
chapters.intro: A stoppered bottle arrives from a former hotel collection, accompanied by a sketch of the demolished courtyard. Bastien recognizes a rain-like impression. Salome does not. The bottle's material history can be investigated without deciding whose memory is correct. A collection label and the sketch's unusual drainage pattern offer two starting points. Bastien puts two blank description cards beside the sample instead of one authoritative caption.
chapters.objective: Choose whether to trace the collection label or examine the courtyard sketch.

choices.label: Trace the collection label
choices.outcome: The accession trail leads to a series of experimental compositions made for the hotel, not a bottle of its actual rain. Bastien marks that distinction before describing the scent publicly. Salome's different impression no longer appears to contradict the object's documented history.
choices.memoryHint: The accession trail leads to a series of experimental compositions made for the hotel, not a bottle of its actual rain.

choices.label: Examine the courtyard sketch
choices.outcome: A rain collector appears beside an old planting bed. The sketch suggests what the original maker may have observed, but not which materials entered the bottle. Bastien asks permission to compare it with the hotel's surviving grounds records.
